articles.title: The biggest questions facing the 7 College Football Playoff title contenders ahead of the 2026 season
articles.summary: The playoff looks wide open as Week 1 approaches.
articles.body:
We think there are seven teams capable of winning the national title ahead of the 2026 college football season.

This year's playoff could be wide open because each of the top teams has at least one big question that needs to be answered over the course of the season. Here are the biggest questions facing our seven contenders ahead of the official start to the season over Labor Day weekend.

The Hurricanes made the national title game a season ago on the back of a dominant defensive front. Edge rushers Rueben Bain and Akheem Mesidor were first-round picks in the 2026 NFL Draft and combined for 22 sacks. That was nearly half of the Hurricanes' 50 sacks in 2025. And Miami doesn't return much of that sack production in 2026.

The pass rush was so good that even nickel Keionte Scott got in on the action with five sacks. He's in the NFL too. The team's leading returning sack leader is defensive tackle Ahmad Moten. He had 4.5 sacks a season ago.

Just like it did at quarterback, Miami took steps to solidify the pass rush in the transfer portal with the addition of former Missouri and Georgia defensive end Damon Wilson II. He had nine sacks for the Tigers in 2025 and should be one of the best pass rushers in the ACC. But he's also the type of rusher who frequents the field on passing downs; Mesidor and Bain were three-down players.

Before 2025, Miami hadn't had more than 37 sacks in a season since 2019. There's likely going to be a drop-off in the sack total this year. If it's precipitous, the Hurricanes aren't going to be national title contenders. If Miami still totals 38 sacks or so, the rest of the defense is good enough to compensate.

The Bulldogs are starting with a near-clean slate at receiver.

After Zachariah Branch was on the receiving end of 81 of the 287 Georgia pass completions in 2025 and players like Dillon Bell, Colbie Young and Oscar Delp are also no longer on the roster, London Humphreys is the leading returning receiver in Athens. He had 18 catches for 276 yards and three scores in 2025.

If Georgia is going to make it back to the SEC title game and contend for the national championship once again, QB Gunner Stockton is going to need players to emerge out wide.

Humphreys should play a bigger role in the offense in 2026. And after him, the Bulldogs are counting on a lot of players without a lot of experience. Redshirt freshmen Talyn Taylor, Tyler Williams and Thomas Blackshear could all play seizable roles in 2026. And there's also true freshman Kaiden Prothro. He's a big target at 6-foot-6, 230 pounds and will assuredly see action in specific packages.

If one or more of those players emerges as a star, Georgia's offense will be in great shape. If they don't, the Bulldogs could end up missing the College Football Playoff altogether.

Just how much better will Texas' pass defense be in 2026?

The entire step back that Texas' defense took in 2025 from 2024 can be traced to its fragilities against the pass. The Longhorns allowed 15.3 points per game two seasons ago. Last year, Texas allowed 20.3. The defense gave up 283 yards a game in 2024. In 2025, that total was 339. That increase was despite opposing offenses rushing for 6 yards fewer per game.

Texas' run defense was stout once again. But the pass defense gave up 51 more yards a game and allowed opposing QBs to complete 3% more of their passes.

It's a massive reason why the Longhorns won three fewer games and failed to make the College Football Playoff in 2025. If Texas is getting back to the 12-team playoff in 2026, the pass defense has to be much more like it was in 2024.

Coach Steve Sarkisian knows that and has rued the big plays his team allowed in 2025. The Longhorns added former Rutgers CB Bo Mascoe in the transfer portal and will give bigger roles to corner Kade Phillips and safety Derek Williams. Don't be surprised if five-star freshman John Meredith III also sees playing time, especially as the season goes on. He reclassified from the class of 2027 after he was ruled ineligible for his senior season of high school.

Who will be Jeremiah Smith's co-star at Ohio State?

The Buckeyes are primed to have wide receivers taken in the top five of the NFL Draft in successive seasons. Junior Jeremiah Smith is a surefire high draft pick if he declares after the 2026 season. This spring, Carnell Tate was the No. 4 overall pick by the Tennessee Titans.

With Tate no longer in Columbus, who will help take attention away from Smith in 2026?

Smith has been one of the best wide receivers in college football since he played his first game in 2024. His stats were down in 2025 and he still had 87 catches for 1,243 yards and 12 TDs. He's going to be QB Julian Sayin's top target. And both players are among the Heisman favorites.

But if Ohio State's offense is going to function at an extremely high level, someone else needs to star alongside Smith and Sayin.

Tate had 51 catches for 875 yards and nine scores in 2025. Overall, the two receivers combined to catch 21 of the 33 TDs thrown by Ohio State QBs. Outside of Smith, only four of those TD passes went to players who are on the Buckeyes' roster in 2026.

Three of them were caught by Brandon Inniss. The senior has a chance to start alongside Smith this season and could post a breakout year after playing behind NFL receivers. Or maybe five-star recruit Chris Henry Jr. breaks out as a freshman. He's the son of the former Bengals and West Virginia receiver. But no matter who it is, Ohio State needs someone to force defenses to not constantly overload coverages toward Smith's side of the field.

Can Indiana's offense average over 40 points a game again?

The Hoosiers have scored over 41 points per game in each of Curt Cignetti's first two seasons in charge. And we don't have to tell you about last year's unit, which averaged 6.8 yards per play on the way to a 16-0 season and the first national championship in Indiana history.

A lot of the players who powered that offense are no longer with the team. Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza was the No. 1 pick in the draft. RBs Roman Hemby and Kaelon Black each rushed for over 1,000 yards and were drafted as well. WR Omar Cooper Jr. was a first-round pick as well and Elijah Sarratt was a fourth-round pick.

That's a ton of production to replace. Cignetti reloaded the offense via the transfer portal again. Can the latest collection of players be just as good?

QB Josh Hoover arrives from TCU and is already among the Heisman favorites after the star turns of Mendoza and Kurtis Rourke before him. Nick Marsh transferred from Michigan State after he had over 50 catches in 2025 and Turbo Richard arrives from Boston College after leading the Eagles in rushing. He'll share duties with Khobie Martin, who had over 500 yards as Indiana's No. 3 back last year. And WR Charlie Becker is back too after his breakout end to the 2025 season.

Indiana has a schedule that should easily make it a playoff team for the third straight year. But if the Hoosiers are going to be more like the team that won three playoff games last year and not the one that lost right away in 2024, the offense will need to be nearly as good as it was a season ago.

How does Notre Dame replace two first-round draft picks at RB?

Fighting Irish QB CJ Carr enters the season as one of the Heisman favorites. And it's easy to see why. If Notre Dame makes another run to the national title game, it's going to be on the shoulders of Carr and the passing offense more than the Irish's rushing attack.

Notre Dame made it to the title game in 2024 after averaging 201 yards a game on the ground thanks to Jeremiyah Love, Jadarian Price and the legs of QB Riley Leonard. With Carr far less of a rusher than Leonard was, Notre Dame didn't get that same running production from the quarterback in 2025, but Love and Price still pushed the Irish to 5.7 yards a carry and over 200 yards a game.

It'll be a surprise if Notre Dame averages two football fields on the ground again in 2026. Aneyas Williams is no slouch — he had over 9 yards a carry in limited playing time last season — and a veteran offensive line will be one of the best in the country. But it's extremely difficult to replace two first-round picks at the same position. A downgrade, even if it's slight, should be expected.

Can Oregon's offensive line be as good as it was in 2025?

The Ducks' front mauled opponents in 2025. Oregon averaged 5.4 yards per carry in 2025 after just 4.4 in 2024. The Ducks' offense averaged nearly 7 yards a play overall and Dante Moore was sacked just 19 times in 15 games.

Center Iapani Laloulu and right guard Dave Iuli are back and have a ton of experience. But they're also Oregon's only two returning starters up front.

Fox Crader should be the starting left tackle after appearing in 10 games as a redshirt freshman in 2025. Fifth-year senior Kawika Rogers could step in alongside him at guard and the right tackle will either be fifth-year senior Gernorris Wilson or Yale transfer Michael Bennett. Don't count out freshmen Immanuel Iheanacho and Tommy Tofi from getting significant playing time, either.

No matter which five players end up as Oregon's starting unit, the Ducks can't afford a big step back if they're going to be the fourth Big Ten team to win a national title in the last four seasons.

articles.title: What to watch: College football Week 1 viewer's guide
articles.summary: The official start to the 2026 college football season is here.
articles.body:
We made it to the official start of the 2026 college football season.

Unlike last year, we don't have a matchup of top-five teams to begin the season. We've got to wait until Week 2 this year. But LSU and Clemson provide us with an intriguing game on Saturday night, and Ole Miss and Louisville on Sunday should also be a fun watch.

Here's what you need to know ahead of Week 1.

If this game is anything like the matchup two seasons ago, Boise State is going to feel really good about its chances of making the College Football Playoff.

In 2024, the teams met in Week 2 with the Ducks taking a 37-34 win on a field goal as time expired. Oregon only beat Ohio State by fewer points in the regular season, as it went undefeated on the way to a Big Ten title. (We won't talk about the Rose Bowl.)

That game turned out to be Boise State's only loss of the regular season as the Broncos went 12-1 and earned the non-power conference berth into the first College Football Playoff.

This year, we're unanimous in believing that Boise State is the favorite to get the Group of Six's playoff berth again. As the headliners of a rebuilt Pac-12, the Broncos can make a big step towards the playoff by avoiding a blowout on Saturday and then taking down Memphis at home in Week 2.

QB Maddux Madsen is back, though he completed fewer than 60% of his throws in 2025 and had a rough outing against Washington in the Las Vegas Bowl. RB Dylan Riley also returns after rushing for over 1,100 yards, but any chance Boise has of upsetting the Ducks will come down to a defense that has seven new starters and had just 27 sacks all season last year.

Oregon, meanwhile, is our pick to win the national championship in January and boasts a Heisman favorite in QB Dante Moore after he eschewed the 2026 NFL Draft. Moore is working with new offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer after Will Stein left to be Kentucky's head coach and was turnover-prone at times in 2025. Even without Stein calling plays, look for Moore, Dylan Raiola and any other Oregon QB who sees time during a game this season to collectively complete over 70% of their throws for the fifth straight season.

During Wednesday's SEC teleconference, LSU coach Lane Kiffin said that Saturday night's marquee matchup had received the most credential requests of any LSU regular-season game and pointed out that both teams were 7-6 in 2025.

Given all that's surrounded LSU and Kiffin since the Tigers moved to hire him at the end of the 2025 regular season, you can understand why. The coach has become the most polarizing figure in college football given the way he left Ole Miss with the Rebels in the College Football Playoff and how he's tried to rebuild LSU's roster. As of Thursday morning, LSU is still waiting to see if it can roster former Ole Miss TE Dae'Quan Wright and ex-Rebels DT Zxavian Harris after the two were cut by NFL teams this summer. Both players were plaintiffs in a Louisiana lawsuit that granted class of 2022 players a fifth year of eligibility after the NCAA didn't extend its new five in five policy to players who were fourth-year seniors in 2025.

LSU added former Arizona State QB Sam Leavitt in the transfer portal and this is his biggest game since the Sun Devils lost to Texas in the College Football Playoff at the end of the 2024 season. Leavitt was limited to just seven games with a foot injury in 2025. His blind side will be protected by former Colorado tackle Jordan Seaton after his transfer to LSU, and the Tigers have former Ole Miss edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen on the defensive line and ex-Boise State safety Ty Benefield in the secondary.

As LSU hit the transfer portal hard, Clemson and coach Dabo Swinney dipped their toes into the portal waters this offseason. But this is still a Clemson roster that's still largely made up of homegrown players. Christopher Vizzina succeeds Cade Klubnik at quarterback and wide receivers T.J. Moore and Bryant Wesco are both back after averaging over 16 yards a catch in 2025.

Chad Morris is back, too. After leading Clemson's offense from 2011-14, Morris returns to be the team's offensive coordinator again after it averaged fewer than four yards a carry. We'll have a great idea of where this Clemson team stands after the first five weeks of the season. The Tigers host No. 7 Miami on Oct. 3.

Wisconsin vs. No. 4 Notre Dame (Green Bay)

When this game was scheduled years ago, it looked like a much bigger game than it actually is. Such is the state of the Wisconsin football program at the moment.

The Badgers are fresh off back-to-back losing seasons for the first time since Barry Alvarez was getting his footing in the early 1990s. Coach Luke Fickell was retained for the 2026 season with an increased commitment to rebuild the roster. Another losing season will likely lead to a coaching search.

Former Old Dominion QB Colton Joseph transferred in to bring some stability to the quarterback position. Wisconsin averaged 136 yards passing per game last season as Week 1 starter Billy Edwards appeared in just two games because of a knee injury. Joseph threw for over 2,600 yards and rushed for over 1,000 last season for ODU.

Fickell said Monday that Wisconsin won't go into the game avoiding Notre Dame CB Leonard Moore's side of the field. That could be a bold strategy. Moore enters the season as one of the best corners in the country and a favorite to be the first defensive player taken in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Notre Dame defense could be the best unit in the country this season with eight other starters back. The Irish return their top six tacklers and the entire secondary.

Offensively, Notre Dame's biggest question is at running back, where Aneyas Williams steps into a starting role following the departures of first-round running backs Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price. Williams averaged over nine yards a carry in limited playing time in 2025. Will the lack of Love and Price mean more pass attempts for QB CJ Carr? He's the preseason Heisman favorite after a breakout redshirt freshman season in 2025.

No. 24 Louisville vs. No. 9 Ole Miss (Nashville)

The Cardinals enter the season with College Football Playoff hopes. And those hopes will become very real with a win over the Rebels.

Louisville avoids Miami and Clemson in ACC play and has SMU, Pitt and Florida State at home. It's a very manageable schedule for an offense that returns RB Isaac Brown after he averaged 8.8 yards a carry on 101 attempts. Louisville also added former Vanderbilt WR Tre Richardson in the transfer portal after he had 806 receiving yards.

QB Lincoln Kienholz transferred in from Ohio State, and his success will hold the key to Louisville's season. Kienholz appeared in 10 games over two seasons with the Buckeyes and has just 36 career passes.

Ole Miss has QB Trinidad Chambliss and RB Kewan Lacy back from the team that made it to the semifinals of the College Football Playoff after Kiffin's departure. Chambliss finished eighth in the Heisman voting and his star only got bigger in the postseason after his performance against Georgia. Lacy led college football with 306 carries and 24 rushing touchdowns in 2025. Can Michigan State transfer Makhi Frazier be a reliable backup and take some of the load off Lacy's shoulders in 2026?

The defense returns Suntarine Perkins, Will Scholes and Kam Franklin and is also boosted by transfers like linebacker Luke Ferrelli — himself a subplot to the LSU-Clemson game — and defensive backs Joenel Aguero and Sharif Denson.

The Seminoles didn't exactly set the world on fire in their Week 0 win over New Mexico State. FSU won 34-17 as a four-touchdown favorite, though it rushed for 217 yards on 39 carries thanks to Ousmane Kromah's 115 yards on just 14 carries. Auburn transfer Ashton Daniels threw an interception, but he also passed for a TD and ran for another.

A win over SMU will ease a lot of the fan base's concerns after the relatively sluggish start to the season. A loss? Well, the unease with Mike Norvell as he enters his seventh season will only continue to fester. Florida State found some ridiculous ways to lose games in 2025, and there's not much margin for error in 2026 with a schedule that also contains Alabama, Louisville, Miami, Clemson and Florida.

The Mustangs are one of the favorites in the ACC and are capable of getting back to the playoff for the second time in three seasons with a healthy Kevin Jennings. The third-year starter was bothered by a foot injury for much of 2025 but still threw for over 3,600 yards. After RB TJ Harden's departure, RB Kendrick Raphael transferred in following a 900-yard season at Cal. The defense will have a lot of new starters but many familiar faces stepping into bigger roles. SMU's opponents have rushed for fewer than 3.4 yards a game in each of the last three seasons.

Colorado at Georgia Tech (-6.5), 8 p.m. ET Thursday (ESPN): Deion Sanders enters a pivotal fourth season with the Buffaloes. Julian Lewis is the team's undisputed starter at QB after he redshirted to end the 2025 season and he has a new offensive coordinator in former Sacramento State coach Brennan Marion. The defense has basically been completely turned over in the transfer portal after allowing over 30 points per game in 2025. Former Indiana QB Alberto Mendoza, the brother of 2025 Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza, makes his first start for the Yellow Jackets and is joined in the backfield by Michigan transfer Justice Haynes.

Liberty at James Madison (-6), Noon ET Saturday (ESPNU): Yes, this game could have serious playoff implications. If either team wants to challenge for the Group of Six spot in the 12-team field, a win is imperative. Jamey Chadwell's Liberty team looks to be the class of Conference USA even after a massively disappointing 4-8 season in 2025. Former Florida coach Billy Napier is back in the Sun Belt after the Dukes made the playoff in 2025. But JMU's roster features very few of the players who played key roles a season ago.

Baylor vs. Auburn (-7.5), 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC): The Tigers' home game was moved to Atlanta after the two teams met in Waco a season ago. Former USF coach Alex Golesh is now in charge at Auburn as QB Byrum Brown followed him to the Plains. Brown was one of the most productive QBs in college football in 2025. Baylor has former Florida QB DJ Lagway in an incredibly pivotal season for coach Dave Aranda.

Tulane at Duke (-7.5), 3:30 p.m. ET (ACCN): The ACC champions begin their title defense against the defending American Conference champ that got into the playoff ahead of the Blue Devils in 2025. San Jose State transfer Walker Eget has been named Duke's starting QB after Darian Mensah's transfer to Miami. Former Houston QB Zeon Chriss-Gremillion will start for Tulane in Will Hall's first game in charge of the Green Wave.

UCLA (-1.5) at Cal, 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN): Is this point spread the Bob Chesney bump? The former JMU coach is now in Los Angeles and his team is a road favorite after a 3-9 campaign in 2025. RB Wayne Knight followed Chesney to UCLA and will serve as the Bruins' primary rusher in 2026 after QB Nico Iamaleava had to do everything for the offense in 2025. Cal has a new coach in Tosh Lupoi, and he convinced QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele to stay in Berkeley for his sophomore season after the Bears went 7-6 in 2025.

Washington State at No. 17 Washington (-23.5), 4 p.m. ET Sunday (NBC): The Apple Cup is not what it once was when both teams were in the Pac-12 and playing each other to end the season. But at least the rivalry is still going, and hopefully it continues for years to come. Kirby Moore is Washington State's third coach in three seasons after Jimmy Rogers' departure to Iowa State. Maybe Moore and the rebuilt Pac-12 can provide the Cougars some stability.

articles.title: TCU restores Fort Worth Star-Telegram credential that was pulled after reporting on locker room fight resulting in player's dismissal
articles.summary: TCU said it revoked the Star-Telegram's credential due to alleged threats made against the player attacked. Reporter Steven Johnson covered the Horned Frogs'...
articles.body:
The TCU football program has restored credentials for the Fort Worth Star-Telegram after the newspaper's access was revoked for its coverage of a locker room altercation that resulted in safety Jacob Fields being dismissed from the team .

"Today, TCU Athletics fully restored media credentials to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram," a statement issued by TCU said . "In a series of productive discussions, we made clear our position and resolved to move forward. We respect their role as an independent news source and voice in our community, and we look forward to the season ahead."

"Today, TCU Athletics fully restored media credentials to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram," a statement issued by TCU said .

"In a series of productive discussions, we made clear our position and resolved to move forward. We respect their role as an independent news source and voice in our community, and we look forward to the season ahead."

Star-Telegram reporter Steven Johnson reported on Aug. 18 that tensions had been developing in the locker room, but coaches made no attempts to de-escalate the situation despite being informed of what was happening. Head coach Sonny Dykes reportedly did not realize how serious the issues were among players.

After the Star-Telegram reported that its credentials had been pulled , a TCU athletic department spokesman said the decision was made because of alleged threats made to sophomore receiver Dozie Ezukanma, who had been punched by Fields. The newspaper's report of the incident did not identify Ezukanma until the player revealed he was the one attacked on a social media video.

Johnson traveled to Dublin, Ireland, to cover TCU's 15-10 loss to North Carolina in its season opener, but did so from the stands rather than the press box at Aviva Stadium.

Jacob Fields dismissed from team after locker room fight

Fields was dismissed from the team earlier this month after the locker room fight. The incident in question occurred Aug. 13.

Ezukanma alleged in an Instagram video that Fields "sucker punched" him, causing his head to hit the floor and knocking him unconscious. He said Fields also kicked him in the head, the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reported .

A TCU football staffer reported the incident to campus police the next day, according to an official report . Fields was subsequently dismissed from the team and a warrant for Fields' arrest stated that Ezukanma suffered a brain bleed from the attack.

Fields was arrested on Aug. 30 after turning himself in to Tarrant County police on a charge of aggravated assault causing serious bodily injury. The senior transfer was booked into the Tarrant County Jail and was released later that day after posting a $50,000 bond .

articles.title: Ipswich Town v Liverpool: How the players rated
articles.summary: How Liverpool and Ipswich Town's players rated following their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Alexander Isak's two early goals set Liverpool on the way to their first Premier League win of the season - and a first for new manager Andoni Iraola - at Ipswich Town .

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

Isak double earns Iraola first Liverpool win

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Kjell Scherpen: Desperately poor for Alexander Isak's early goal. Weak and meant Ipswich got off to the worst possible start. A couple of decent saves but the damage was done. 4

Dara O'Shea: Led from the front as always but Ipswich's defence struggled against the movement of Isak and the creation of Gakpo. He had a hard time. 5

Issa Diop: Towering figure always willing to indulge in the physical changes but this was a tough night after those two early Liverpool goals. 6

Jacob Greaves: Stern test against the inspired Cody Gakpo, showing the quality he will face in the Premier League. 5

Leif Davis: Tested defensively but was always competitive. Lent weight to attacks and had a chance with a far post header. 6

Sasa Lukic: Will bring experience to Ipswich Town but on this night Liverpool 's midfield was too powerful. 5

Exequiel Palacios: Tried to bring some composure to Ipswich Town 's game but was fighting a losing battle. 6

Abdul Fatawu: Pace but little end product. Energetic but erratic. 5

Julio Enciso: Ipswich's main threat. Tireless. Might have done more with the final ball but never gave up even when odds were against him. 7

Daizen Maeda: Anonymous. Made no impact at all and no surprise when taken off. 5

Emersonn: Battled hard but no luck against Van Dijk and Jacquet. 5

Jack Clarke (on 66 Maeda): Introduced when the game was lost. 5

Zian Flemming (on 66, Emersonn): Couple of bustling contributions. 5

Subs not used: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Florentino, Nunez

Alisson: Lucky to get away with misjudging a first-half corner. The occasional anxious moment but no harm done. 6

Ronald Araujo: Strong in the air and on the ground on an impressive Premier League debut at right-back. Important interventions by being in the right place at the right time. 7

Virgil van Dijk: Usual unruffled self in the face of some frantic Ipswich Town attacking. 7

Jeremy Jacquet: Solid alongside Van Dijk. Continues to look a very fine acquisition. 6

Milos Kerkez: Occasionally troubled by Fatawu's pace but never in huge difficulties. 6

Dominik Szoboszlai : Driving runs from midfield and always willing to test the keeper. Iraola should never use him at right-back. 7

Alexis Mac Allister: Still not quite at his best. Too many misplaced passes but never hides or shirks responsibility. 6

Florian Wirtz: Busy but occasionally lightweight. As so often, showed subtle touches that hint at good things to come. 6

Alexander Isak: The best of Alexander Isak at last. Running behind a defence with pace and clever movement with cool finishes. Finally showed why Liverpool bought him. 8

Victor Munoz: Willing and pacy out wide but could have delivered more end product. 6

Cody Gakpo: Could have been playing for Manchester City . How glad Liverpool are he wasn't. Two superb passes for Isak's opening goals, Truly outstanding performance. 9

Bradley Barcola (on 64, Munoz): Showed one or two flashes of the lightning pace the £123m signing will bring to Liverpool . 5

Ryan Gravenberch (on 64, Isak): Brought on to shut down any potential Ipswich Town revival.

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Frimpong, Tsimikas, Endo, Ngumoha

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: David Beckham, Wayne Rooney and Newport's Harrison Biggins: The long-shot kings
articles.summary: After Harrison Biggins' 70-yard goal, BBC Sport Wales recalls some of the best long-range strikes over the years.
articles.body:
David Beckham and Wayne Rooney are famous for their long-range goals, but Newport County's Harrison Biggins has eclipsed even their best efforts.

Biggins' screamer in Newport's 2-1 defeat at Salford City has been measured at exactly 77.7 yards, which may well be an English Football League (EFL) record.

The sensational effort might even put Beckham's 59-yard stunner for Manchester United at Wimbledon in 1997 in the shade.

It also surpasses in distance Rooney's remarkable 61-yard goal for Everton at West Ham United in 2017.

Fans of League Two Newport are no strangers to applauding long-range 'worldie' goals.

Their former goalkeeper Tom King proudly boasts the Guinness World Record distance for a goal scored in a competitive football match - an astonishing 105-yard effort for Newport at Cheltenham in 2021.

BBC Sport Wales takes a look back at some of the furthest goals ever scored.

Where else could this list start, but with the World Record holder Tom King.

When Newport faced Cheltenham in blustery conditions at the Jonny-Rock Stadium in 2021, even King himself could have not expected what would follow.

The now-Everton stopper prepared to take an ordinary goal-kick.

But aided by the wind, his strike travelled the length of the pitch, bouncing over Cheltenham goalkeeper Joshua Griffiths and into the net.

It was the first time a goalkeeper had scored in a match in the English Football League since Barry Roche for Morecambe against Portsmouth in 2016.

King later admitted that even he didn't know how to celebrate the moment as he surpassed Asmir Begovic's previous record of 100.5 yards.

Moritz Stoppelkamp, SC Paderborn (91 yards)

If King owns the overall record, then Moritz Stoppelkamp's effort for Paderborn is the longest ever scored by an outfield player.

Paderborn were leading Hannover 1-0 in a Bundesliga match in September 2014 when the visitors committed everyone forward in search of a late equaliser, including goalkeeper Ron-Robert Zieler.

After the danger was cleared, the ball dropped to Stoppelkamp on the edge of his own penalty area.

With one touch to set himself, he unleashed a stunning strike on the volley from 83 metres (91 yards), into the unguarded net.

The effort set a new Bundesliga distance record, surpassing Giorgos Tzavellas' previous mark by 10 metres - more than 13 yards further than Biggins' strike.

Harrison Biggins, Newport County (77.7 yards)

Biggins' effort may not have threatened King's world record or be the furthest scored by an outfielder, but it has already secured a place among the EFL's most memorable long-range goals.

Newport County were under pressure against Salford City when the midfielder collected possession deep inside his own half.

Rather than simply clearing his lines or threading Shaquille Gwengwe in on goal, Biggins took a touch, beat a man and, spotting Norris well off his line, unleashed a rocket.

His stunning effort sailed over the stranded Norris and nestled in the net, prompting jubilant celebrations from the travelling supporters.

Unfortunately for Newport , the goal ultimately came in a 2-1 defeat after Salford staged a late comeback.

But it was further evidence of a player who has never been afraid to attempt the ambitious.

Newport boss Hayden Mullins has seen the midfielder attempt that kind of spectacular effort three times, the first a near-halfway lob against Roma in pre-season and the second striking the post from a 40-yard volley against Bristol Rovers.

"The goalkeeper was pretty high out the box and if there's one person who's going to try that, it is him," said Mullins.

"I didn't expect him to score, but it is a fantastic goal."

Salford rally late to sink Newport for first league win

Fleetwood into top half with win at 10-man Newport

Breaking down Chelsea's staggering 39 summer exits

Biggins' strike stands at almost 20-yards further out than Rooney's tremendous strike at Goodison Park.

But what made Rooney's that little more special was that it clinched the former England striker's first hat-trick in more than six years.

As Joe Hart dispossessed the onrushing Dominic Calvert-Lewin, he could do little to prevent the ball falling to Manchester United's all-time record goalscorer.

And when it fell at Rooney's feet, he made no mistake in drilling the ball over everyone and into the net.

A fine strike for a man who scored 366 career goals, but few more memorable than this.

Though not known for his goalscoring ability, netting just 16 times during his five-year spell at Liverpool, Xabi Alonso always had an eye for the spectacular long-range attempt.

Even he admits that his brilliant strike at St James' Park to give the Reds a 2-0 victory against Newcastle United is the best of his career.

The ball broke to the current Chelsea boss just inside his own half and having seen keeper Steve Harper off his line, his audacious effort from just over 60 yards nestled in the back of the net.

Harper in his scramble to get back slipped and could only watch in wonder as the ball sailed over his head.

It was the second time in a year that Alonso had scored from inside his own half, having found the net against Luton in the FA Cup in January that same year – so Newcastle cannot say they were not warned.

Josh Windass, Sheffield Wednesday (around 60 yards)

Current Wrexham man Josh Windass has always had the ability to shoot from range.

But none of his goals compare to the 60-yard strike he hit on New Year's Day, which ensured 2025 opened with a bang for Sheffield Wednesday supporters.

Running on to a loose ball inside his own half, the Owls forward took one touch before spotting goalkeeper Jacob Zetterstrom off his line and sending a remarkable effort looping into the far corner.

It sparked memorable celebrations at Hillsborough, but not from Windass, who instead soaked up the applause in his usual nonchalant demeanour , allowing himself just one wry smile.

David Beckham, Manchester United (57 yards)

No list of long-range goals would be complete without this man's name.

The goal that propelled Beckham into the headlines was one of the most impressive the Premier League era has seen.

The opening day of the season. Selhurst Park, 57 yards out, last minute. A ball broke to Beckham who - as has been a common theme throughout these goals - spotted goalkeeper Neil Sullivan off his line, went for the spectacular.

His inch-perfect attempt lobbed Sullivan and, in a career in which the former England captain scored 127 goals, this 57-yard lob against AFC Wimbledon perhaps ranks as his greatest strike.

Biggins' effort, scored during a wet and windy Tuesday night League Two encounter, will not attract the acclaim of the renowned goals from Beckham, Alonso or Rooney.

But the former Shrewsbury Town man may well have written himself in the EFL history books with his phenomenal 77.7-yard strike.

articles.title: Doblete tempranero de Isak da la victoria al Liverpool
articles.standfirst: Alexander Isak firma un doblete para anotar la primera victoria de la temporada del Liverpool
articles.summary: Alexander Isak firma un doblete para anotar la primera victoria de la temporada del Liverpool
articles.body: Nueve minutos tardó el Liverpool en firmar la victoria pues el temprano doblete de Isak puso por delante a los Reds frente a un Ipswich sin opciones. Andoni Iraola apostaba por los titulares del último partido frente al Nottingham Forrest a excepción de la titularidad de Ronald Araujo. En el banquillo de al lado, Gary O'Neil presentaba igualmente un único cambio en el once inicial frente a la derrota de Old Trafford. Los Reds buscaban su primera victoria esta temporada y se ponían el mono de trabajo para conseguirlo. Los goles no tardaban en llegar. Un doblete de Isak en apenas nueve minutos ponía el resultado a favor de los rojos. Generando peligro y cogiendo el ritmo de juego que le ha faltado al Liverpool en las dos jornadas previas, es como insistía el conjunto de Anfield para mantener la ventaja hasta el descanso. Los segundos 45 minutos se presentaban de la misma manera. Mucho dominio Red y disparos desafortunados de los Blues. Enciso disparaba en múltiples ocasiones pero Alisson no se equivocaba. El Liverpool seguía jugando a lo suyo, llegar al área y amenazar la portería local. Dos disparos de Szoboszlai obligaban a Scherpen a sacar los puños. El guardameta de O'Neil evitaba la goleada. Los cambios llegaban y el debut de Bradley Barcola con él. La banda izquierda era su pista pero el centro hacia Gakpo no encontraba la red. El Ipswich perdía posesión muy rápido y aunque Clarke intentó un disparo, este golpeó en su compañero Diop y ni rozó los tres palos. Un posible penalti podría haber supuesto el tercero para los de Iraola pero el fuera de juego previo a la falta sobre Szoboszlai cambiaba la dirección de la jugada. Fueron cinco de añadido, pero ni eso fue suficiente para cambiar el pronóstico que se preveía desde los primeros minutos. El Liverpool consigue anotar los tres puntos en Portman Road ante un Ipswich con pocas amenazas que llegasen al área Red. El siguiente enfrentamiento liguero para los de Anfield será en casa ante el Fullham de Arbeloa.

articles.title: World Cup review: FA to canvass England players in analysing tournament
articles.summary: The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament.
articles.body:
The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament.

English football's governing body has started the post-tournament review they conduct after every major international competition. The FA says the review is the standard process it undertakes after all tournaments.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel and members of his backroom team were at St George's Park last week where they were involved in unpacking their performance in north America with a wider report into the team's World Cup campaign to be delivered at a later date.

And it is understood members of Tuchel's squad will be spoken to, and their feedback taken into account, as part of the review process.

The players' involvement in the review provides an interesting dynamic given the emerging sense from members of the World Cup squad that Tuchel's substitutions and tactical approach contributed to their semi-final loss to Argentina - despite taking a 1-0 lead through Anthony Gordon.

BBC Sport revealed in the 24 hours after that defeat that at least three senior players privately expressed misgivings about Tuchel's approach in the closing stages of the game.

There was a widely held view that Tuchel's changes and tactical set-up were too defensive late on as they conceded two late goals to lose 2-1.

The ongoing review will also look into the impact of the team's permanent Kansas City base during the tournament.

After every game, they returned to Kansas City - and the effects of the travelling will be analysed.

England went on to defeat France in the bronze medal match to record their best World Cup finish since lifting the trophy in 1966.

With that in mind, key figures at the FA view the tournament as a success and the organisation has backed Tuchel before the Euro 2028 qualifying campaign.

England will play their first game since the World Cup in the Nations League against Spain on 26 September. They will also face two matches in the tournament against the Czech Republic, either side of playing Croatia, during the next international window.

articles.title: El Madrid no puede perder este partido
articles.standfirst: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.summary: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.body: Así es. Primera derrota del Real Madrid. Primera derrota de José Mourinho. Fatal. Una derrota que no entraba en los pronósticos, aunque el Madrid no le había ganado al Betis en su casa en las cuatro últimas temporadas. Pero, las cosas como son, lo diga Agamenón o su porquero, el Madrid no puede perder este partido. Lo tenía que haber ganado por lo civil o por lo criminal (mejor lo primero, claro), como sucedió con el Espanyol. Se deja tres puntos importantes que le va a costar mucho recuperar. ¿Y por qué no ganó el Madrid este partido? En primer lugar, no mereció perderlo, aunque el empate tampoco habría evitado este mal sabor porque a día de hoy un empate es casi una derrota. Y no lo ganó el Madrid por varias circunstancias. Una: un segundo tiempo malo de verdad, con mucho control pero sin ideas arriba. Dos: Mbappé fue decisivo...para mal. En el primer tiempo falló la ocasión más clara de todo el partido ¡por dos veces! Y en el minuto 93 falló un penalti que no debió haber fallado. Para eso él es el gran especialista. Tres: Alvaro Valles, portero del Betis, fue el héroe del partido, no sólo por el penalti parado (los penaltis se fallan, no se paran, como decía el gran Puskas) sino por varias jugadas más, entre otras una en el primer tiempo en la que evitó el 0-1 de Huijsen (tras un pase, cómo no, de Arda Güler). Cuatro: Bellingham no apareció...cuando parecía por sus últimos encuentros que estaba en un gran momento de forma. Cinco: Vinícius no se fue de nadie. Provocó el penalti, es cierto, pero está muy lejos de ser el Vinicius al que se le ha dado el Himalaya por renovar su contrato. Seis: la marcha de Arda Güler, seguramente por tener una tarjeta amarilla y para evitar que el equipo se quedase con diez en la segunda mitad. Lo que ocurre es que al irse Güler se fue también el Madrid. Mourinho tiene claro qué cambios tiene que hacer y cuáles no hacer. En fin, una derrota que duele. Y duele porque no se veía venir. El Madrid de Mourinho ha dejado de ilusionar de golpe. Y el martes le espera el Inter. Una prueba de fuego

articles.title: Hamburger SV vs. 1. FSV Mainz 05 preview: Both teams look for first goal and win
articles.summary: Hamburg entertain Mainz in the penultimate matchday 2 game of the Bundesliga as the two teams are yet to register their first goal of the campaign.Hamburger...
articles.body:
Hamburg entertain Mainz in the penultimate matchday 2 game of the Bundesliga as the two teams are yet to register their first goal of the campaign.

HSV bosses were busy closing deals on deadline day after HSV's poor showing in the first Topspiel of the season. Merlin Polzin's side were thoroughly dominated by Borussia Dortmund despite the respectable 2-0 scoreline.

However, the excitement is palpable ahead of the first home game of the season after they signed three players in the final hours of the transfer window. Fábio Vieira signed on a permanent deal after his impressive season on loan, while Zakaria El Ouahdi and David Møller Wolfe arrived at Volksparkstadion to fill the gaps in fullback positions.

HSV's latest signings are all candidates to improve last week's lineup. However, Louis Lemke will hope to make his full debut at Volksparkstadion weeks after becoming the first 16-year-old to score for the club.

On the contrary, Mainz did their business early in the market. The 05ers even allowed Andreas Hanche-Olsen and Marco Richter to depart late without signing replacements. The former joined Robert Lewandowski at Chicago Fire, while Richter is now a free agent after they agreed on a contract termination.

Urs Fischer's side looked to be a bit weak in squad depth compared to last season, but there will be no European nights this time around. The experienced coach started the campaign with a goalless draw with newly-promoted Paderborn last week.

Dominik Kohr, who suffered a late injury against Paderborn minutes after coming close to breaking the deadlock, is out of the game. Eric Martel has to wait longer for his Mainz debut, but Stefan Posch is now ready for the starting lineup.

HSV recorded their biggest victory back in Bundesliga in this fixture last term. Rayan Philippe, who has now joined Paderborn on loan, scored twice in a 4-0 victory against Bo Svensson's men. With Fischer in charge of Mainz in the return fixture, star figures Nadiem Amiri and Fábio Vieira were on target as the sides shared the spoils at Mewa Arena.

articles.title: Ohio State vs. Ball State Buckeyes Wire staff predictions for Week 1
articles.summary: It's Week 1 of the college football season and Ohio State kicks it off against Ball State. Our Buckeyes Wire staff predicts the score, and why.
articles.body:
There's no better time of the year in Columbus, Ohio, than college football season, and after a long wait and a loss by Ohio State to Miami (FL) in the College Football Playoff , the Buckeyes are ready to get back on the field when they host Ball State at 12:30 p.m. ET on Saturday in the 'Shoe.

The oddsmakers -- heck, almost anyone without a Ball State degree (and even most with one) believe this one will be over shortly after scarlet and gray colors step off the bus. The Cardinals are traveling from Indiana to take on the preseason No. 1 team , and there is talent oozing out of all corners of the Ohio State roster.

But the game must be played, and so we'll keep an eye on several things as we get to see this year's Buckeye squad for the first time in 2026. For years now, we like to have our Buckeyes Wire writers take turns predicting the score of each OSU game with a little synopsis of what things will look like, so here we go with Week 1.

Ohio State hasn't lost a season-opening game since it lost to Miami (FL) back in 1999. Consider that streak very safe against a Ball State team that is coming off of a very rough year and just doesn't have the athletes and depth to compete with the talent the Buckeyes have.

There might be a little rust for OSU, but the players and coaches will shake it off early enough and score in bunches on the way to a blowout win. It'll be a great time to get some depth pieces in the game and rest the starters for what's coming next week against Texas .

Score Prediction: Ohio State 52, Ball State 7

The Buckeyes get a tune-up game before heading to Austin. Never overlook an opponent, but Ball State is one of the bottom dwellers of the Mid-American Conference. The forecast is calling for rain, which may be the only thing that can slow down the OSU offensive attack. Unfortunately for the Cardinals, a little weather won't be enough as the Buckeyes roll.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 42, Ball State 3

Ohio State enters the game on Saturday with sky-high expectations once again as the No. 1 team in the country. Ryan Day may want the Buckeyes to get to a strong and early lead so they can let their younger players get snaps in preparation for the top-5 showdown the following week in Austin.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 49, Ball State 3

It's the start of a new season, and there's a lot of optimism around what this Ohio State team can be. Julian Sayin and Jeremiah Smith are the obvious storylines, but this could arguably be one of OSU's most talented rosters top to bottom in the last few years. There are a lot of young and promising stars who will look to build on successful early-season performances. Because of that, and the fact that it's Senior Day, I expect nothing short of a terrific outing from the Buckeyes. Things may take a bit longer to click offensively with new OC Arthur Smith , but the excitement level is there. Slow start into a dominant overall performance. Ohio State rolls.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 56, Ball State 6

articles.summary: Some strong backing from a man who knows the youngster well.

Xavi Espart has been making waves at Barcelona this season after starring for Hansi Flick's side in the first three games of the new La Liga campaign.

articles.title: 49ers got a 16-hour flight to Australia. Here's how my journey compared
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers got a direct flight to Melbourne from SFO with lay-flat seats. For a new reporter flying coach, connecting through New Zealand, it wa...
articles.body:
Before their season opener across the globe on Thursday, the San Francisco 49ers flew to Melbourne, Australia, a week before kickoff. The team departed San Francisco late Wednesday night and arrived in Australia early Friday morning (local time) in an effort to adjust their body clocks well ahead of game day.

While the 17-hour time difference between California and Melbourne after a 16-hour flight sounds daunting, was the experience actually that bad? Here's what we learned, and here's how my travel experience compared to that of the 49ers.

The 49ers were chartered on a nonstop, 16-hour United Airlines flight from San Francisco International Airport to Melbourne. Players, coaches and executives were treated to luxury lay-flat seats where they could stretch their legs, rest their heads on a pillow and enjoy a semi-legitimate sleeping experience.

That sounds nice. Although maybe not nice enough to meet the standards of certain players. Offensive tackle Trent Williams said Wednesday morning in Santa Clara, hours ahead of the 49ers' flight, that the standard lay-flat seats for players on road trips are not that comfortable for anyone over 6-foot-1.

"Hopefully we get something a little bit bigger than that," Williams said, "or it's gonna be torture."

It appears some 49ers got adequate rest. In an interview with local Australian TV station 10 Sport, offensive lineman Enrique Cruz Jr. (6-foot-5, 313 pounds) and defensive tackle Gracen Halton (6-foot-3, 293 pounds) said they slept 11 hours and "the whole time," respectively.

Kicker Eddy Piñeiro , on the other hand, said on the Australian Football League broadcast that he remained "a little jet-lagged" Friday night after sleeping just a couple hours on the flight.

I dare Williams - or any other Niner, for that matter - to attempt my flying experience. I flew economy on Air New Zealand with a layover in Auckland. On my first flight - a 12-hour trip from SFO to Auckland before another four-hour flight to Melbourne - I slept four hours. I couldn't recline my seat more than two inches. The $15 memory foam neck pillow I bought in the international terminal's convenience store offered some pillow-like characteristics, but my head remained upright the whole night.

The saving grace was that the middle seat in my row remained vacant. My aisle seat suddenly had a decent amount of legroom, and I used it to my advantage, stretching my legs into the open space under the middle seat. The window seat passenger in my row smartly pushed down the armrest and used most of the middle seat as her personal foot rest.

On the first flight, we received two hot meals: one "dinner" early in-flight and one "breakfast" as our 6 a.m. Auckland arrival approached. In case I hadn't eaten enough breakfast, I got another one on my second flight to Melbourne, since that one took off around 9 a.m. local time.

After landing Friday morning, our next big challenge was beating the jet lag. The 49ers seemed to do it better than I did. The team had a training session and a few welcome events the afternoon of their first day (Friday). At night, San Francisco players attended an Australian Football League match between the Geelong Cats and Carlton Football Club at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, the 100,000-capacity stadium in which next week's game between the 49ers and Rams will be played.

Good on them for putting in a full day's work in the new time zone. After checking into my hotel and exploring the Southbank Riverwalk in downtown Melbourne in the late afternoon, I passed out at 8 p.m., not long after sunset.

Safe to say - as I write this story wide awake at 5 a.m. Saturday in Melbourne - jet lag is no joke. Although it was a challenging travel experience, one thing is certain: The 49ers will be well-adjusted by game time.

The Los Angeles Rams , on the other hand? They're expected to arrive about 24 hours before kickoff. Best of luck to them.

articles.title: Revealed: Real reason PSG star Joao Neves was seen driving around white delivery van despite earning eye-watering salary
articles.summary: Football News: PSG star Joao Neves arrives at training in a modest Peugeot van filled with presents for the PSG Foundation, demonstrating his humility and generosity despite earning €175,000 weekly.
articles.body: Joao Neves raised a few eyebrows when he turned up at Paris Saint-Germain training this week driving a rather ordinary white Peugeot van.For a player reportedly earning €175, 000 a week,approximately $205,000, the sight of the 21-year-old arriving behind the wheel of a 2021 Peugeot Partner, believed to be worth around $10,000, was always going to get people talking. Footage quickly spread online, with supporters wondering why one of PSG's biggest stars had chosen such an unglamorous set of wheels.It turns out there was a very good reason.Neves had filled the van with presentsThe Portugal international was not simply making a particularly modest choice of transport. According to PSG influencer Djaameel, Neves had packed the back of the van with hundreds of presents that he intended to donate to the PSG Foundation, which distributes support to disadvantaged children.Also read: Joao Neves earns £150,000 a week and has won 2 Champions League titles - so why does he drive a £7,000 van?Djaameel shared the explanation on social media after the footage of Neves arriving at the training ground began circulating."For info, João Neves did indeed arrive at the Campus in a van, but there was a reason behind all that. A reason that commands even more respect and demonstrates what a remarkable human being he is," he wrote."The double European champion had hundreds of items in the back of his van that he donated to the charitable works of the PSG Foundation!"The post added: "This just goes to show how incredible, humble, and team-spirited he is."So the apparently humble vehicle had a rather less humble load in the back.Neves joined PSG from Benfica in 2024 and has quickly established himself as an important part of Luis Enrique's midfield. He has already collected two Ligue 1 titles and two Champions League trophies with the French club and has also been named in the Ligue 1 Team of the Year once.A landmark PSG appearance could be nextNeves' charitable gesture comes as he approaches another milestone with PSG.He missed the club's recent 2-2 draw with Lille because of illness, but is expected to return to the squad when PSG host Monaco in Ligue 1 on Friday night.If he is fit enough to play, the appearance will be his 100th for PSG since arriving in the French capital two years ago.It would be quite a landmark for a player who has made such a rapid impact in Paris. Neves' work rate and determination have made him a key part of Enrique's side, while his trophy cabinet has filled up rather quickly for someone who only turned 21.And now there is another little detail attached to his PSG story: when the club star turned up at training in a van that looked more suited to a delivery round than a Champions League winner, there were actually hundreds of gifts waiting inside.Not quite the glamorous arrival some fans expected, perhaps. articles.title: Deion Sanders Reacts to Shedeur Attending Colorado's Season Opener in Emotional Video After Win
articles.summary: Colorado football head coach Deion Sanders understandably got emotional while talking about what it meant for his son, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders, to attend the Buffaloes' 14-13 season-opening win over Georgia Tech in Atlanta and walk off the field with him on Friday evening.
articles.body:
Colorado football head coach Deion Sanders understandably got emotional while talking about what it meant for his son, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders, to attend the Buffaloes' 14-13 season-opening win over Georgia Tech in Atlanta and walk off the field with him on Friday evening.

Report: Clemson Warns LSU of Contract Breach

"Y'all see a coach, you see Prime, you see someone that has dealt with success in certain areas of life," Sanders said, per Bri Amaranthus of Colorado Buffaloes on SI. "Some of them have made a multitude of mistakes as well. But y'all forget, like, I'm a real loving, caring father. And that's my son, man. So I feel it."

Shedeur Sanders, who will start this season as the Browns' backup quarterback, is getting ready for the beginning of Cleveland's 2026 campaign, which kicks off on Sunday, Sept. 13 at the Jacksonville Jaguars. But the ex-Colorado signal-caller (2024 and 2025) took some time to visit his old team on Friday. Sanders was quite happy.

"For him to, you know, get out of practice and make it to this game, I think he's going to fly back with us," Sanders said. "He's going to spend a couple days with his dad. Like, I love that."

Sanders, who is a father to two daughters and three sons, also spoke about what fatherhood meant to him.

"I love fatherhood. I love fatherhood. I really do," Sanders said. "I wasn't fathered like I'm a father. So some people can take the wrong and keep it going wrong. Some people can take the wrong and make it right."

Colorado enjoyed a thrilling win in Atlanta. The Buffaloes were down 13-7 with 1:40 remaining, but quarterback Julian Lewis drove his team 75 yards in 1:03 capped by a 20-yard touchdown pass to tight end Charlie Williams.

Georgia Tech stormed right back and gave itself a chance with a 45-yard field goal attempt, but defensive back Boo Carter came through with a huge block to preserve the win.

And with that, Deion and Shedeur Sanders got to walk off the field in victory.

Colorado's next game will be Saturday, Sept. 12 at home against Weber State.

articles.title: Court Ruling Allows 2 Starting Defensive Linemen to Play for No. 6 Indiana Against North Texas
articles.summary: BLOOMINGTON, Ind. (AP) — No. 6 Indiana will have two starting defensive linemen from their national championship team, Stephen Daley and Kellan Wyatt, on the field Saturday for its opener against North Texas following a court ruling Friday night.
articles.body:
BLOOMINGTON, Ind. (AP) — No. 6 Indiana will have two starting defensive linemen from their national championship team, Stephen Daley and Kellan Wyatt, on the field Saturday for its opener against North Texas following a court ruling Friday night.

Indiana circuit court Judge Kara Krothe of the Monroe Circuit Court in Bloomington issued a temporary restraining order barring the NCAA and its conferences from prohibiting any of the case's seven plaintiffs from competing in Division I athletics in 2026-27.

Daley and Wyatt each were granted a fifth year of eligibility in a previous court decision.

Judge Clears Path for Ex-NFL Players to Join LSU

Report: Clemson Warns LSU of Contract Breach

Daley led the Big Ten with 19 tackles for loss last season after he moved into the starting lineup midway through the season but missed the College Football Playoff after suffering a season-ending knee injury during the Big Ten championship postgame celebration.

Wyatt started the first seven games last season and had 28 tackles, eight for loss, and 2 1/2 sacks before suffering a season-ending knee injury last October.

Neither player was drafted and neither signed with a pro football team as undrafted rookies.

Their eligibility had been in doubt since an Aug. 21 from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit that overturned a lower court's ruling that granted an additional season of eligibility to the high school graduating class of 2022.

Daley and Wyatt were allowed to practice with the Hoosiers with their status in jeopardy, and coach Curt Cignetti said the school and the program would support both players as they continued to battle in court.

Indiana faced a similar situation with starting defensive back Louis Moore last summer. He was allowed to compete in the Hoosiers first two games before eventually being allowed to play the entire season, and he became a key cog on a defense that helped the Hoosiers win their first national championship and become the first major college football team with a 16-0 record since the 1890s.

The current case in Monroe Country also involves former Indiana basketball player Malik Reneau, now at Miami, an Indiana women's volleyball player, two Hoosiers swimmers and a Butler University basketball player.

Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney made some history... and an early case for his Heisman Trophy candidacy on Friday.

The star wide receiver broke Eddie Brown's single-game Miami record with 233 receiving yards against Stanford, per Tim Reynolds of The Associated Press. Brown recorded 220 yards in a game in 1984.

Toney also recorded three touchdowns against the Cardinal.

Here's a look at his final box score stats and highlights from Miami's 45-6 win over Stanford.

Toney opened up the No. 7 Hurricanes' season-opening matchup against Stanford with a touchdown on Miami's opening drive. He promptly hit the Heisman Trophy pose in the end zone after opening the scoring.

Toney followed that up with another touchdown on Miami's second drive of the game. You can take a guess as to what pose he hit in celebration:

And if that wasn't enough, Toney scored his third touchdown of the game in the third quarter to put Miami up 42-6 on Stanford. Enter another Heisman celebration:

Naturally, fans and pundits alike have already put Toney on Heisman watch as a result:

Toney is coming off a productive 2025 campaign, as he led the country with 109 receptions.

His 1,211 receiving yards and 10 touchdown catches also were the most among all ACC players last season.

Toney particularly excelled during Miami's College Football Playoff run, which ended in the national championship game. During the Hurricanes' final two CFP contests, he caught 15 passes for 203 yards and two touchdowns.

With Toney now playing alongside new Miami quarterback Darian Mensah, expectations are high for him.

Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal previously praised Toney during ACC media days in July.

"All you can really say is that guy is special. I've never seen anything like him," Cristobal said, per 247Sports' David Lake . "Normally a receiver with his talent and production is a diva. Special player and elite human being."

articles.title: ‘You cannot compare it to our era’: Cafu on Brazil’s decline, 28-year World Cup drought and India clash
articles.summary: Football News: Navi Mumbai: His words were in Portuguese. His expression, however, reflected love and happiness, just like how he played the game.Standing on stage, .
articles.body: Navi Mumbai: His words were in Portuguese. His expression, however, reflected love and happiness, just like how he played the game.Standing on stage, as he addressed the enchanted students of Pillai University here, Cafu soaked in the adulation. The smile on his face was constant and matched the one of him in the background poster with that enduring image — of him holding aloft the 2002 FIFA World Cup trophy.More than 24 years later, the hair on his head may have thinned. His popularity clearly hasn’t, judging by the increasing decibel levels as he spoke to the young gathering, many of whom came dressed in Brazil’s iconic canary jersey.The excitement all around peaked when the Brazilian great showed off some of his skills in a brief ball-juggling exchange with India international Nikhil Poojary.A small sample perhaps of a bigger Brazil-India clash coming up in Kolkata next month, when Khalid Jamil’s side host the five-time world champions in an international friendly.The high-profile fixture has been the topic of debate. What will India, ranked as low as 138th, truly stand to gain from taking on a footballing giant? A fair bit, according to Cafu.“Well, if you go by the rankings, there is a significant difference between Brazil and India, but football has modernized. Today, everyone plays on equal terms,” the charismatic former AC Milan and Roma right back told reporters later. “You saw this in the World Cup. In the World Cup, national teams like Curacao, teams like Cabo Verde, played on equal terms with all the big national teams.“We hope that Brazil and India can play a great game. It will bring many benefits to the Indian people and to the Indian national team, which will face a team that is a five-time world champion. I think establishing this connection between these countries, now that FIFA has expanded the World Cup, opening up space for other countries, will be important for India as well.”But what about Brazil? How does the only man in history to play in three consecutive World Cup finals explain the decline of the once-mighty Selecao ever since he led them to their fifth star that evening in Yokohama 24 years ago?“We see that every change is necessary in football. Brazil has been going through a difficult period when it comes to the national team, because it has been more than 24 years — completing 28 years by 2030 — without winning a World Cup title,” Cafu, now 56, said.“You cannot compare it to the era when we played, when we played in three consecutive World Cup finals. That was an era that has passed. It is a new generation, they are new players, and we have to root hard so that this new era and these new players can achieve what we achieved: reaching a World Cup final.”But even under one of the game’s most decorated coaches in Italian Carlo Ancelotti, a man Cafu knows very well, the challenge of returning to the pinnacle of world football remains complicated, the two-time World Cup winner pointed out.“The World Cup is not an exact science. The best do not always win, and the champion is not always the best team. It is a sequence of factors that makes you win a World Cup,” said Cafu, who won the UEFA Champions League in 2007 with AC Milan under Ancelotti’s watch.“I am very hopeful when talking about the Brazilian national team. I hope Brazil can win the World Cup in 2030 now and end this 28-year drought.”Asked whether the growing trend of Brazilian talent moving to Europe’s footballing elite prematurely was, in some way, to blame for the national team’s struggles, Cafu felt conflicted over the argument.“I am biased to speak because when I played my third consecutive World Cup final, I was playing in Italy,” he said.“This is very relative. All national teams, except for the 1994 team, had the majority of their players playing outside the country, playing in other teams that were not Brazilian clubs.“Today, young Brazilian players are leaving earlier for other countries, and because of that, perhaps they do not develop an identity with the Brazilian national team, an identity with the Brazilian people. Perhaps that is what is missing most for our Brazilian national team: a bit more Brasilidade (Brazilianness) in these players—feeling the weight of what it means to play for a Brazilian club, going to the Brazilian national team, and only then going abroad to another country.”Hailed as one of the game’s greatest full backs, Cafu, who enthralled fans with his charging runs up and down the right flank, said modern-day tactics meant the position today didn’t quite offer players the same freedom.“Everything has changed in our position. In our time, the full-back was a full-back. He covered the midfield, covered the wings, went to the far post, crossed and came back.“I, as a full-back, ran 22 km in one match. That was the intensity with which we played,” Cafu said. “Today, I see that most wingers are having a little more difficulty, because most of the coaches are playing with systems that restrict the full-back's overlapping runs and prevents them from reaching the byline.“But we were stubborn wingers. We didn't listen to what the coach said and liked to play. That's why we attacked and defended with the same intensity.”Towards the end of his media interaction, the broad smile appeared once more when one asked Cafu whom he would choose, if he had to pick between Ronaldo, his former Brazil teammate, and Lionel Messi? “Ronaldo fenomeno,” he grinned.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jayden Maiava Dazzles, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from USC Win vs. Fresno State
articles.summary: Jayden Maiava dazzled in the USC Trojan's dominant 39-0 shutout over the Fresno State Bulldogs on Friday, making the Trojans the first team this season to secure two victories
articles.body:
Jayden Maiava dazzled in the USC Trojan's dominant 39-0 shutout over the Fresno State Bulldogs on Friday, making the Trojans the first team this season to secure two victories

USC entered Friday as a heavy 21.5-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook , after a Week 0, 42-26 victory over the San Jose State Spartans, living up to the hype behind its seasoned quarterback.

Heading into halftime at home, Maiava and the Trojans had put 30 points on the scoreboard behind a clean first half from their senior quarterback, who accounted for three touchdowns while completing 94 percent of his passes.

Maiava was pulled after one unsuccessful drive in the third quarter, following an impressive Week 1 showing.

Prior to Week 0 action and USC's 16-point victory over the Spartans, ESPN's Jordan Reid projected Maiava to be selected in the third round of the 2027 NFL draft, alongside a handful of other notable picks, including LSU's Sam Leavitt and Oklahoma's John Mateer.

Meanwhile, on Friday, ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. projected at least five quarterbacks to be selected in the first round, including the USC quarterback.

"Beyond Moore and Manning, I feel most solid on Notre Dame's CJ Carr, Miami's Darian Mensah and USC's Jayden Maiava going Day 1 ... right now ," Kiper wrote.

With an impressive half and then some, Maiava only saw his stock rise before he was sent to the bench for the remainder of the game, allowing the Trojans to ride out the rest of the victory.

Maiava and the Trojans opened the game with an 82-yard, 12-play drive that ended with a short connection from Maiava to Tanook Hines for a touchdown.

USC's defense came up big on the following play, coming away with an interception, but the Trojans could not turn it into points, fumbling to close out the first quarter.

Maiava found Trent Mosley twice for touchdowns in the second quarter before Waymond Jordan rushed up the middle for a score, giving the Trojans a 30-0 lead.

Meanwhile, the USC defense stood tall, forcing two punts, a safety and a fumble in the frame.

Maiava was pulled after USC fumbled the ball with 5:20 remaining in the third quarter, and freshman Jonas Williams stepped in for the remainder of the game.

Looking to build on its momentum, USC will host the Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns next Saturday.

articles.title: New LSU Rumors Reveal Lane Kiffin's Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris Roster Decision for Clemson Game
articles.summary: LSU didn't add tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris to the team's roster for a season-opening clash with Clemson on Saturday, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.
articles.body:
LSU didn't add tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris to the team's roster for a season-opening clash with Clemson on Saturday, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel .

Thamel noted that both players could potentially be added later in the year, as they're enrolled at the school.

On Thursday, a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in their eligibility case that paved the way for players such as Wright and Harris to suit up in college for a fifth year after spending time in NFL training camps.

Report: Clemson Warns LSU of Contract Breach

However, Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger reported that Clemson general counsel Chip Hood sent a brief email to LSU's general counsel in which he brought up "certain eligibility" issues that may break "contractual obligations between the two parties."

The SEC and ACC were among several conferences that recently implemented rules to prevent players that previously declared for the NFL draft and did not withdraw consistent with NCAA requirements or signed a contract with an NFL team or another professional league from returning to play in college.

Wright reached an agreement with LSU for the 2026 season after clearing waivers upon his exit from the Cleveland Browns, while Harris committed to the Tigers after he was waived by the New Orleans Saints.

Although the SEC filed a lawsuit against LSU with a U.S. District Court in Alabama on Thursday alleging that the school violated the league's "First Amendment right of expressive association" by ignoring the new rules that prohibit the addition of former NFL players, the preliminary injunction still allowed Wright and Harris to play.

They won't be on the field when LSU and Clemson face off on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET, though.

articles.title: LSU leaves Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris off Week 1 roster despite court ruling in Tigers' favor
articles.summary: LSU reversed course, opting to leave Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris off its roster in 2026.
articles.body:
When LSU takes the field against Clemson on Saturday, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris will not be with the team. Both players — who were subject to various legal challenges over their eligibility — were left off LSU's Week 1 roster when the team submitted it to the SEC on Friday, according to ESPN.

After various arguments and legal filings, LSU earned a major victory Thursday , as a judge ruled in favor of Harris and Wright against the SEC. In doing so, the judge paved the way for LSU to include both players on its 2026 roster, even though that would go against the SEC's wishes.

But despite that court ruling, LSU ultimately decided not to risk the ire of the SEC or other conference members, leaving Harris and Wright off the roster. For now. The players can still be added to the roster at any point during the season since they are already enrolled at the university. LSU has two open roster spots.

A lawsuit — filed by the SEC against LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin on Thursday — may have influenced the school's decision. In it, the conference argued both LSU and Kiffin "waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes to play football for LSU during the 2026-27 season, including players who had signed NFL contracts with the Cleveland Browns, New Orleans Saints, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers."

In the lawsuit, the SEC asked to be allowed to enforce its First Amendment rights to tell members to comply with its rules. In an attempt to prevent players with professional experience returning to college, the SEC and various other conferences adopted a policy in August that would ban the practice.

But, crucially, that policy did not apply to Harris and Wright, who had already received a temporary-restraining order from a judge, allowing them to return to college in 2026. In the aftermath of the SEC's attempt to ban the tactic, Kiffin initially said LSU would comply with that ruling . But as it became clear Harris' and Wright's situation was not as clear cut, Kiffin said he would wait and see how Thursday's ruling turned out before making a call.

That decision opened the door for Kiffin to add both Harris and Wright to LSU's roster Friday night if the school wanted to test the conference. Both players have experience in the NFL, as Harris signed with the New Orleans Saints in May, and Wright saw time with the Philadelphia Eagles and the Cleveland Browns before they were cut and signed with LSU.

While it seemed like Kiffin wanted both players on his roster during the legal process, he (or LSU) apparently decided it wasn't smart to go against the SEC at the last second given everything that has unfolded this week.

As part of Thursday's ruling, the judge " enjoined LSU from taking action to prevent the players from competing ," per Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger. Leaving Harris and Wright off the roster could lead to future legal battles if their absence continues for weeks.

Had Harris and Wright been put on LSU's roster, the school would have potentially faced retaliation — or more legal challenges — from the SEC or its members, which were reportedly furious over LSU's attempt to use pro players.

articles.body:
Two of the Premier League's early strugglers meet at Craven Cottage on Saturday, with Fulham and Crystal Palace both still without a win after two rounds of fixtures.

Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham sit 16th following defeats to Chelsea and Sunderland, while Pierre Sage's Palace are 18th after losing to Everton and being beaten 4-1 by Manchester City. Both clubs are still finding their feet under new head coaches this season, with Sage having replaced Oliver Glasner in the summer and Arbeloa taking over from Marco Silva.

History favours the visitors here: Crystal Palace have not lost at Craven Cottage in the league since January 2005 and have won their last three trips to Fulham in all competitions, most recently drawing 1-1 at Selhurst Park in January.

Both sides strengthened on deadline day, too, with Fulham adding midfielders Hugo Larsson and Manuel Angel plus defender David Affengruber, while Palace brought in Ben Chilwell, Quinten Timber, Honest Ahanor and Dario Osorio.

Fulham vs Crystal Palace – Match preview and team news

Last meeting: Crystal Palace 1-1 Fulham (Premier League, 1 January 2026)

Tom Cairney is the only absentee, ruled out with a long-term knee injury. Deadline-day arrivals Hugo Larsson, Manuel Angel and David Affengruber are all available but unlikely to start, with Alvaro Arbeloa saying fans should "be patient" as they adapt. Shea Charles could come into the side in place of Oscar Bobb, with Gonzalo Garcia continuing to lead the line after scoring twice in his first three appearances.

Jean-Philippe Mateta will miss around three weeks with a hamstring injury, while Ismaila Sarr remains sidelined and Chadi Riad continues a long-term absence with a knee problem. Deadline-day signings Honest Ahanor, Ben Chilwell, Quentin Timber and Dario Osorio are all in contention but unlikely to be thrown straight into the starting side. Adam Wharton, who stayed despite transfer interest over the summer, continues in central midfield.

Fulham have lost both their Premier League matches so far, beaten 3-2 by Chelsea before going down 1-0 at Sunderland, though they did register a 3-0 EFL Cup win over AFC Wimbledon in between. The visits of Liverpool and Manchester United follow this fixture, adding urgency to Arbeloa's search for a first league win.
