Leeds United head to the south coast off the back of an unbeaten start to the season, looking to end a wretched record at the Amex Stadium when they take on Brighton & Hove Albion on Saturday.

Daniel Farke's side have taken four points from their opening two Premier League matches, while Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton sit on three points after contrasting results at either end of the season so far.

The two sides met on the penultimate weekend of last season, when a 96th-minute Dominic Calvert-Lewin goal secured Leeds a 1-0 win at Elland Road. Brighton, though, have the upper hand historically on home soil, unbeaten in their last ten home league meetings with the Whites and having kept eight consecutive clean sheets against them at the Amex.

Leeds, remarkably, have played more matches without winning at this ground than any other in their history. Both clubs strengthened on deadline day, with Brighton adding Chema Andres and Femi Azeez, and Leeds bringing in Melvin Bard and Jean-Matteo Bahoya.

Brighton vs Leeds United – Match preview and team news

Venue: The American Express Community Stadium

Last meeting: Leeds United 1-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Premier League, May 2026)

Jack Hinshelwood, Yankuba Minteh, Kaoru Mitoma, Mats Wieffer, Stefanos Tzimas and Evan Ferguson are all sidelined through injury, with Wieffer not expected back until after next month's international break. Georginio Rutter and Yasin Ayari are doubts after missing last weekend's defeat at Chelsea. Costinha could make his first start at right-back in Wieffer's absence, and new signings Chema Andres and Femi Azeez are both in contention to feature in some capacity.

Joe Rodon will miss eight to ten weeks with what Daniel Farke described as a "serious hamstring injury," while Mateo Joseph also remains out with a knee problem. Ilia Gruev has returned to training and could be involved in some capacity, and new arrivals Melvin Bard and Jean-Matteo Bahoya are both available, having joined on deadline day. Nico Elvedi is set to deputise for Rodon and could earn his first Premier League start.

Brighton's season has swung between extremes: a 4-0 opening-day thrashing of Aston Villa followed by a 4-3 defeat at Chelsea, making them only the second English top-flight side since 1950 to score four in their opener and then concede four in their next game. Hurzeler's side have also dominated possession in both matches, and a third successive 70%-plus display would set a new record for the start of a Premier League campaign.

Leeds remain unbeaten this season, following a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest with a battling 1-1 draw at home to Brentford, in which Calvert-Lewin's late leveller salvaged a point after a below-par first-half display. Farke's side have already matched two of their away wins from the whole of last season in all competitions, a marked improvement on their travels.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham Hotspur – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest and Tottenham Hotspur meet at the City Ground on Saturday, both still searching for their first win of the season. Oliver Glasner’s Forest...
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest and Tottenham Hotspur meet at the City Ground on Saturday, both still searching for their first win of the season.

Oliver Glasner's Forest picked up a point in a 2-2 draw at Liverpool last time out, while Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham slipped to a 2-0 home defeat against Newcastle United, leaving them without a goal after two matches for the first time in Premier League history.

Both clubs enter the fixture off the back of significant summer rebuilds. Forest made six additions, including Colombia wing-back Daniel Munoz and club-record signing Liam Delap, while Tottenham spent close to £400m on ten new arrivals, the last of whom, Mykhaylo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo, joined from Chelsea on deadline day. History favours the hosts on paper: Forest have won each of their last four Premier League meetings with Spurs, most recently a 3-0 victory at Tottenham in March.

Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham Hotspur – Match preview and team news

Last meeting: Tottenham Hotspur 0-3 Nottingham Forest (Premier League, 22 March 2026)

Nicolo Savona remains the only long-term absentee, though Oliver Glasner confirmed he has returned to partial training and could be involved after the international break. Ibrahim Sangare has recovered from the calf knock that ruled him out at Liverpool and is available again. New signing Daniel Munoz is fit to play at right wing-back despite limited pre-season minutes, while Liam Delap, who made his first appearance off the bench against Liverpool, continues to build match sharpness.

James Maddison trained on Thursday but will not be involved on Saturday, still working his way back from a shoulder injury. Savio has recovered from the muscle problem that kept him out against Newcastle and is available, while deadline-day loan signing Mykhaylo Mudryk is fit enough for a substitute appearance of up to 30 minutes rather than a start. Mohammed Kudus, who made his first appearance since January off the bench last time out, may be considered too soon to start again.

Forest have taken one point from their opening two league matches, losing to Leeds United before fighting back from behind twice at Liverpool, only to be pegged back on both occasions in a 2-2 draw. Home form remains a concern, with Forest having lost both of their fixtures at the City Ground so far this season and won just one of their last twelve Premier League home games.

Tottenham remain without a point after defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, conceding five goals and scoring none in the process. It is the first time in the club's Premier League history that they have failed to score in either of their opening two matches, and a defeat on Saturday would be their first three-match losing start to a top-flight season since 1979-80.

articles.title: Malachi Toney catches 3 of Darian Mensah's 5 TD passes in No. 7 Miami's Week 1 rout of Stanford
articles.summary: Toney topped his career-high in receiving yards in the first half of Miami's blowout win.
articles.body:
Malachi Toney made it very clear that he plans on being a Heisman Trophy contender on Friday night.

The sophomore wide receiver scored three touchdowns and set a career-high in receiving yards in No. 7 Miami's 45-6 win over Stanford. Toney's previous career-best was a 146-yard effort. He eclipsed that total in the first half, with nine catches for 174 yards and two scores.

He then capped his night with a 47-yard TD catch after splitting Stanford's cover-two defense down the middle to make Miami's win all but official. He struck the Heisman pose after that score, just like he had following his first two touchdowns.

Toney finished the game with 12 catches for 233 yards.

After playing with Georgia transfer Carson Beck in his first season of college football, Toney caught passes Friday night from former Duke quarterback Darian Mensah. After leading the Blue Devils to the ACC title in 2025, Mensah got a big offer from Miami at the end of the season and reneged on his commitment to return to Duke to head south to play for the Hurricanes.

His first game in a Miami uniform went pretty well. Before exiting the blowout in the third quarter because the game was out of reach, Mensah had more touchdown passes (five) than he had incompletions (three). Mensah finished the game 27-of-30 passing for 400 yards.

Of course, it's easier to post a stat line like that when Toney is just running away from defenders. Mensah had a very good game too — but Toney was absolutely uncoverable. Stanford's defense was helpless to keep up with him. Nearly every completion to Toney came with him having significant separation from the nearest defender.

A season ago, Toney had 109 catches for 1,211 yards and 10 receiving touchdowns. He burst onto the scene in his first college game with six catches for 82 yards and a TD in the Hurricanes' win over Notre Dame and had three receiving TDs across Miami's four College Football Playoff games.

That breakout season made him one of the few non-quarterbacks among the favorites for the Heisman ahead of the season. While Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith enters the 2026 season as the top non-QB in the Heisman betting odds, Toney was the No. 2 player who doesn't regularly throw passes.

Friday night made it clear that Toney's chances for the Heisman are very real. Mensah's are too. Miami is the clear favorite to win the ACC and get back to the College Football Playoff. And if both players play simply close to how they did in Week 1, the race for the ACC may not be all that close.

articles.title: Troy produces a dominating season-opening victory over Amsterdam
articles.summary: Troy, a football team that lost in the 2025 Super Bowl against Niskayuna, opened its 2026 season in style Friday with a resounding 47-8 victory over Amsterda...
articles.body:
TROY - Anthony Brown emerged from a team huddle in the end zone following the conclusion of the Troy High football team's season-opening contest Friday night vs. rival Amsterdam. Brown, a junior quarterback making his first varsity start, had ample reasons to be sporting a wide grin of satisfaction. He played well and, more importantly, the Flying Horses breezed to a lopsided win.

Troy dominated on offense, defense and special teams in registering a thorough 47-8 home victory over the Rugged Rams in Section 2 Class A action.

Last year, Troy finished 8-3 overall - a season in which it reached the Super Bowl and beat Amsterdam 34-28 to win the Capital Division title. Friday, they routed the Rugged Rams by scoring touchdowns on four possessions during the first half.

"Amsterdam is one of our biggest rivals and a team we don't like. The score should have been a lot greater. We're not really satisfied," Troy senior running back/linebacker Vulonn Forde said. "Next week, we're planning to come harder."

"Honestly, this was pretty great. I think there is more to expect," Brown said.

Troy outgained Amsterdam 303-101 in yards and even that was a bit misleading because the Flying Horses' defense created a number of short drives for the offense. The host team opened five series on Amsterdam's side of the field and scored touchdowns on all five possessions.

"All of these guys were so hungry to get out here. To do what we did today, and knowing that we can improve in so many areas still is something they all know," Troy coach Jordan Canzeri said.

Essentially, the only two things the Troy coaching staff could find fault with after the game ended was taking too many penalties and one play in the second quarter when Brown tried to avoid a sack and ended up taking a 29-yard loss.

Troy (1-0 overall, 1-0 Class A) scored twice in the opening quarter as senior running Nymiear Jenkins scored on a 1-yard touchdown run and Brown connected with Deonte Raysor for a 31-yard touchdown pass.

Forde later scored on the first of his three touchdown runs when he galloped untouched into the end zone from 16 yards out to establish a 20-0 advantage.

Amsterdam (0-1, 0-1) responded with its lone scoring drive of the game when Jonathan Rosario on a fourth-down run from one yard out following a fumbled snap.

Jenkins capped the scoring in the first half when he reached again, this time on a 6-yard touchdown run from the Wildcat formation.

"Everybody on the field on both sides of the ball - all of my teammates - played their hearts out," Forde said.

Forde added touchdown runs in the third quarter covering 26 and 22 yards, respectively, and Kieonte Green dashed 68 yards down the right sideline for the game's final touchdown on a punt return.

"I can't be proud enough of just the trust they have and all that they have done so far to this day," Canzeri said of his team.

Forde displayed unique power for a player who stands 5-foot-8 and weighs 178 pounds. The senior, who surpassed the 1,000-yard plateau as a sophomore and junior, broke several runs after being hit by multiple defenders. The same went for Jenkins.

Brown, who went 6-for-6 passing in the first half, finished 7 of 11 for 115 yards and one touchdown. He said the exploits from Forde and Jenkins, along with the stellar work all evening turned in by the offensive line, made his job easier.

"We probably have the two best backs in the section, so every time they touch the ball they get five to 10 yards. That opens up the pass," Brown said.

Troy's defense recorded four sacks and Green added a second-half interception. The Rugged Rams were limited to only six yards rushing.

articles.title: Fran Fernández, el español que es líder con Ucrania aún en guerra: "Ojalá lo mantengamos en el tiempo"
articles.standfirst: El ex de Almería, Alcorcón y Murcia ha colocado al Karpaty Lviv en la cima de la clasificación
articles.summary: El ex de Almería, Alcorcón y Murcia ha colocado al Karpaty Lviv en la cima de la clasificación
articles.body: Francisco Javier Fernández Díaz (Almería, 1980) decidió dar un giro radical a su carrera cuando en enero aceptó una oferta para dirigir al Karpaty Lviv. Ni la guerra de Ucrania le echó para atrás. "Creo que acerté plenamente", asegura a MARCA. Ahora, "después de un inicio complicado", ha colocado a los 'leones' en una situación privilegiada. A la espera de recibir al 'todopoderoso' Shakhtar Donetsk, son líderes con 10 puntos de 12 posibles. "Ojalá lo mantengamos en el tiempo", desliza. Que así sea. Pregunta. Ha dirigido a Almería, Alcorcón, Tenerife y Murcia. ¿Qué es lo que le llevó a firmar con el Karpaty Lviv en enero? Respuesta. Llevaba tiempo queriendo tener una experiencia fuera y después de la decepción por lo que había pasado en Murcia [el equipo se quedó a las puertas del ascenso] consideré que era el momento de salir fuera de España. Apareció el Karpaty, un proyecto deportivo que me llenaba, con buenos medios para trabajar y la verdad es que, después de un inicio complicado, creo que acerté plenamente. La intención de salir era vivir la experiencia no sólo profesional, sino también a nivel personal: mejorar mi inglés, crecer y aprender también de otras culturas. Estoy encantado en ese aspecto. P. Su primera aventura en el extranjero le lleva hasta Ucrania, un país, que, aunque ya no abra los telediarios, continúa en guerra. ¿No le dio miedo asentarse en Lviv con los bombardeos que sigue sufriendo el país? R. Antes de firmar estábamos preocupados, por eso viajé antes, para poder comprobar cómo era esto, de primera mano. También hablé con varios españoles que estaban ya aquí y dentro de la situación complicada, sus referencias eran buenas. Una vez aquí, empecé a ver y vivir lo que estaba ocurriendo. Es cierto que en el día a día no lo noto, no se percibe tanto que estamos en guerra. En esta ciudad es más fácil. Hay otras donde la situación es más compleja, pero aquí no. Por ejemplo, aquí, tanto en los partidos en nuestro estadio como durante los entrenamientos, nunca ha sonado la alarma [la que previene de los ataques o los bombardeos]. En casa, ya de noche, durmiendo, sí que ha sonado alguna vez de madrugada. Pero bueno, como te digo, en esta ciudad, en el día a día, en la calle, cuando la gente hace su vida no se nota casi nada que el país esté en guerra. P. El Shakhtar, por ejemplo, lleva más de 10 años lejos de Donetsk y se ve obligado a jugar la Champions en Stamford Bridge. Tiene que ser difícil adaptarse a tantos inconvenientes. R. Es duro decirlo, pero es así, hay momentos en los que el ser humano parece adaptarse a todo. Salvando las distancias, me recuerda a la época del Covid en España, cuando nos acostumbramos a una vida extraña, pero seguíamos adelante. Aquí llevan cuatro años y medio de guerra y cada uno trata de hacer su vida: el ocio es aparentemente normal, la gente sale muchísimo de casa e incluso cuando hace frío ves a gente en las terrazas, paseando, dando una vuelta. Creo que la gente quiere olvidarse también de la situación que se está viviendo. Sí que es cierto que hemos viajado a alguna ciudad donde el escenario es más complicado y sí que hay más restricciones. Por suerte, y por ello también elegí venir aquí en Lviv, que está cerca de la frontera con Polonia, la situación en el día a día es bastante normal. P. Hablemos de fútbol. Llegó en enero y lo cierto es que esta temporada no podía haber comenzado mejor. ¿Imaginaba verse líder después de cuatro jornadas con 10 puntos de 12 posibles? R. No, en absoluto. Sí que esperaba que el equipo diese un paso adelante que es lo que buscábamos. Esos primeros meses de adaptación me vinieron muy bien para conocer el fútbol ucraniano, conocer la mentalidad… Y bueno, darle nuestro toque personal. Sí que esperaba estar entre los siete u ocho primeros que era el objetivo que se había marcado el club. Respecto al liderato actual, ojalá lo mantengamos en el tiempo. Ahora tenemos que jugar contra el Shakhtar [hoy a las 17.00, hora peninsular española], un equipo duro, fuerte y que juega en Champions. P. Le espera el Shakhtar, como dice, pero años atrás el Karpaty Lviv, con Lucas Pérez a la cabeza, llegó a competir en Europa. ¿Hasta dónde se puede soñar con llegar esta temporada? R. Yo siempre he sido de ir paso a paso y de objetivos cercanos. Innegablemente la gente está muy ilusionada. ¡Se han vendido todas las entradas en dos horas! Viene el Shakhtar, que como digo juega Champions League, que es un equipazo y que cuenta con un presupuesto muchísimo mayor. En cualquier caso, tenemos una ilusión tremenda y, sobre todo, tenemos confianza. Tengo la tranquilidad de haber empezado bien la temporada y tengo confianza en el equipo. No me pongo metas, de verdad, vamos a ir partido a partido y el objetivo que tenemos ahora es intentar ganar el sexto partido (ganaron en Copa de Ucrania). P. Su balance de goles es abrumador: 11 a favor y sólo dos en contra. ¿Cómo definiría su propuesta futbolística? R. Intento adaptarme a los jugadores que tengamos. La temporada pasada, cuando cogí el equipo, estaba en una dinámica negativa, con muchos goles en contra y había que cambiar eso. Lo primero que hicimos fue reforzar al equipo en defensa. Tuvimos seis o siete partidos con portería a cero, de hecho, fuimos el equipo menos goleado en la segunda vuelta. Ahora nos toca dar un paso más en el aspecto ofensivo, en el ataque. Y es lo que estamos intentando hacer, ser un equipo más valiente, más vertical, incisivo… Intentamos siempre construir el juego desde atrás, con mediocentros con buen pie, para tener buena construcción de juego. Y luego, sobre todo, me gusta que los jugadores de arriba sean verticales, jugar con extremos y delanteros que le den profundidad al equipo. Para mí, jugar bien es tener más ocasiones que el rival y es lo que estamos intentando consolidar. P. Tiene en plantilla a cinco españoles, alguno que contaba con gran cartel en categorías inferiores. ¿Qué le aportan, respectivamente, Moha, Bruno Iglesias, Iván Calero, Joaquinete y Xeber Alkain? R. Cosas muy diferentes. A Moha lo conozco del Murcia, lo tuve allí. Jugador de cantera en el Real Madrid y Barcelona. Es un futbolista que, técnica y tácticamente, para mí es top. Aporta mucha inteligencia en el centro del campo, siempre quiere el balón y para mí, es muy importante. Bruno Iglesias es una promesa, no sólo del fútbol español, sino europeo. Creo que es un jugador que todavía no ha competido a nivel profesional pero que tiene unas características que, sí sigue evolucionando, puede ser muy importante. En las categorías inferiores del Madrid ha sido un jugador con influencia en el juego y le falta dar ese pasito que espero que lo dé con nosotros. Iván Calero nos aporta experiencia y profundidad en el lateral. Es un jugador que también lo tuve en Alcorcón y que conocía perfectamente. Es un gran profesional y nos aporta muchísimo. Joaquinete, a pesar de ser español, ya lo considero muy ucraniano [ríe] porque lleva tiempo aquí en Ucrania. Fue uno de los jugadores más importantes la temporada pasada en la Liga. Un jugador que nos aporta goles y desequilibrio en la parte de arriba, igual que Xeber Alkain por la otra banda, son jugadores parecidos. Xeber está totalmente adaptado, vino en enero y también hizo una segunda vuelta bastante buena. Es un futbolista que, sobre todo, nos da esfuerzo en banda y desequilibrio. P. Para terminar, a nivel personal, ha vivido un verano duro con la pérdida de su madre. ¿Cómo sacó fuerzas para venir a Almería y sólo unas horas después regresar a Ucrania para dirigir al equipo? R. Se mezcla, sobre todo, un sentimiento de responsabilidad y de culpabilidad por no estar más cerca de la familia, en Almería, en estos momentos difíciles. Desde luego que no es fácil manejar situaciones tan duras estando a tantos kilómetros de distancia. Sin embargo, sé que mi familia entiende mi trabajo, me apoya y respeta, y yo trato de seguir con mi vida y mi carrera. Ahora lo que toca es trabajar duro. Por supuesto, también por ellos, por el beneficio de mi familia.

articles.title: Septiembre ha empezado explosivo
articles.summary: Comprimidos, por Juan Ignacio Gallardo
articles.body: E l mes arranca calentito. El Madrid se va por primera vez a la lona. Un gol anulado y un penalti fallado sellan el primer tropiezo de los de Mou. Faltaban las primeras polémicas y las primeras dudas sobre el equipo. Ya están aquí. § Luis de la Fuente se ha echado España a la espalda. Y ni tan mal. § Lo que ha ocurrido en el caso de Julián Álvarez es insólito: todas las partes implicadas han salido perjudicadas. Todas. § Ha caducado el axioma de Enrique Cerezo: Los futbolistas ya no juegan donde quieren. Casadó, Pablo García, la ‘Araña’... § La pasada semana viajé al futuro. Estuve en el impresionante campus y laboratorio que Huawei tiene en Shenzhen, megalópolis vecina de Hong Kong. Allí, además de explicarnos en detalle los atributos del Watch GT 7, un innovador reloj focalizado en deporte y salud que acaban de lanzar, nos mostraron el deslumbrante (y apabullante) abanico de productos tecnológicos que esta inmensa compañía global tiene -y tendrá- en el mercado. Conclusión: en China van por delante de la vanguardia. § En este enriquecedor periplo, que tuvo extensión a la hipnótica Shanghai, coincidí con un interesante grupo de creadores de contenido que hicieron aún más ameno el viaje. Tuve ocasión de conocer de cerca a @Sarabace, @csantaengracia, @candelaperez, @emilio_alcaraz, @raulgb_01... destacados referentes en el fascinante e infinito territorio digital. Nunca he entendido los recelos que muchos periodistas convencionales tienen ante los influencers serios. Observando desde primera línea cómo trabajan uno comprueba enseguida que son grandes profesionales, con enorme talento, imaginación, creatividad, conocimiento y una gran capacidad de comunicación. Y no es nada sencilla su labor. Detrás de cualquiera de sus contenidos hay mucho tiempo de preparación, guionización, grabación, edición... Todos ellos tienen una llegada, un alcance, un predicamento y una conexión con sus comunidades (que suman millones de seguidores) que resulta envidiable para la inmensa mayoría de periodistas. En sí, estos ‘content creators’ son personas singulares, inteligentes, dotadas de ingenio, agudeza y unas cualidades humanas cautivadoras. En uno de los múltiples aeropuertos del trayecto nos hicimos una foto. “¡Pero tienes que sacarla en el MARCA!” me pidieron. Y -al igual que cantó Sabina- yo que siempre cumplo un pacto, cuando es entre caballeros, les tenía que escribir este artículo. Un verdadero placer conoceros, chic@s. § La convocatoria se completó con Zuo, Shawn, Cristina, María, Sergio, Eugenio, Jon, Xoaquín, Félix... Equipazo.

articles.summary: El conjunto franjirrojo llega con tres incorporaciones del último día de mercado. En el Racing, Iker Luque no viaja por una sanción acumulada
articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano regresa a Butarque para ejercer de local ante un Racing de Santander que ya sabe lo que es sumar tres puntos en una jornada. Un duelo repleto de nuevas caras en ambos conjuntos tras el cierre del mercado de fichajes, en el que parece que muchos de ellos pueden debutar con sus nuevos clubes. Beñat San José tiene pendiente la victoria. A pesar de que el Rayo Vallecano ha comenzado todos los encuentros de esta liga poniéndose por delante, le han conseguido remontar en dos ocasiones e igualar en una. La última, después de encajar cinco goles frente al Barcelona y en la que mostró una imagen algo endeble en defensa. Con hasta tres nuevas caras en la plantilla que se oficializaron el último día de fichajes, el cuadro franjirrojo quiere volver a la senda de la victoria en Butarque y deberá hacer frente a un recién ascendido en otra de esas pruebas claves por la permanencia. El Racing cerró de forma brillante el mercado de fichajes y ahora queda que José Alberto pueda engranar a los jugadores para conseguir el objetivo de la permanencia. Las últimas incorporaciones han entrado en la lista que viajan a Madrid salvo Iker Luque que arrastra sanción. Ante el Rayo Vallecano el técnico racinguista apostará en principio por un once plagado de jugadores que llevan trabajando con el equipo desde hace tiempo, salvo en la banda derecha del ataque donde Iker Luque y Andrés Martín son baja, por lo que no es descartable que podría debutar Pablo García de inicio. Camello vs Zabiri. El delantero franjirrojo llega a este duelo tras anotar un gran doblete en el Camp Nou, aunque insuficiente. Su rival será el marroquí, que no se quedo atrás, y anotó un memorable hat-trick en el Sardinero ante el Elche. Ambos prometen tener buenas ocasiones de gol paraa seguir sumando tantos. Seguir sin contar con Vallecas puede pesarle al Rayo. El conjunto franjirrojo necesita victorias en este comienzo de LaLiga, pero su complicada puesta en escena en Butarque y el buen momento del Racing pueden ser suficientes motivos de peso para que se deje puntos.

articles.title: Man Utd made midfield recruitment a summer priority, so what happens now?
articles.summary: Michael Carrick says Manchester United have balance in their midfield following a £150m summer recruitment campaign - so who plays?
articles.body:
Michael Carrick struck a chord with many Manchester United fans as he lavished praise on Kobbie Mainoo after his side's thrilling 5-2 victory over Ipswich at Old Trafford, calling the midfielder's performance "immense".

Starting in the Premier League for the first time since he surprisingly failed to play a minute at the World Cup, Mainoo caught the eye with his performance and Carrick made sure the 21-year-old was not overlooked on a day skipper Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick.

But former United goalkeeper Ben Foster had a different take.

"I love Kobbie," Foster wrote on his Threads account.

"He's the future, but he's not there yet. Be honest with yourself and you'll know he's not gonna be one of the first four or five names on the team sheet.

"If he can get a year out on loan where he is the main man, where he is needed and relied upon every single game, that will instil something in him he won't get at Manchester United."

The social media reaction suggested Foster had got it wrong.

There are plenty of people who feel Mainoo absolutely should be one of the "first four or five names" in Carrick's side.

But, if that was correct, what would it mean for the three international midfielders United have spent more than £150m on this summer after identifying it as a priority area?

Carrick is about to feel the impact of United's qualification for the Champions League.

Last season, United had two midweek games in the second half of the season. They drew at West Ham and lost at Newcastle. They then had 13 and 11-day gaps to their next fixture respectively.

Starting with their trip to Everton, United have five games in 16 days before the first international break of the campaign.

If Carrick's side progress in the EFL Cup, they won't have a spare midweek until Christmas.

Rotation is inevitable in United's new-look midfield this season - but what will that look like?

In assessing the signings that have been made, Carrick speaks about balance.

Brazil midfielder Casemiro left at the end of his contract while Uruguyan Manuel Ugarte - likely to leave anyway had he not suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury during the World Cup - is out until next year.

That left Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes and Mason Mount as United's only senior central midfielders going into the summer transfer window, with the latter pair better suited to more advanced roles.

After missing out on Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes, United moved quickly to sign Brazilian Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £48m. A day later, Belgium's 29-year-old Youri Tielemans joined from Aston Villa for £35m.

Santos, 22, dovetailed well with Mount during the early pre-season games, sitting deep and screening the back four.

Mount played in the number eight role and seemed to be a viable option to stay there into the new campaign until an ill-timed injury at the beginning of August provided a reminder of his unhappy record of absences.

Tielemans' pre-season appearances seemed to be based around developing an understanding with skipper Fernandes.

"Andrey, for such a young man, to come in the way has, with his character and his personality is a dream," Carrick explained when he spoke to reporters during his side's training camp in County Kildare.

"He's so positive, so mature, so switched on; he wants to learn. He comes in and straight away he's trying to help other players, talk in games and communicate. He's got a real substance to him.

"Youri's a little bit more obvious, probably because we've seen an awful lot of him and we all know him, but again, the character, the personality, the presence, and the quality on top.

"The two midfielders in particular, will give us an awful lot moving forward."

At £70m, the Cameroon international is in the top 10 of United's most expensive signings of all time. It is the kind of fee, in the club's new era of restraint, that suggests he should also be one of the "first four or five names on the team sheet".

Each player adds something different to United's midfield.

Baleba provides speed, aggression and defensive awareness.

Tielemans has comfort on the ball, plus his passing and vision.

Santos excels in one-to-one duels. He also has defensive awareness, a good passing range and used short bursts to break defensive lines.

Mainoo's ability comes through his willingness to take the ball in tight spaces and progress it up the field.

It is a formidable array of qualities but they cannot all play at the same time.

"You sound like you're in our coaches' office trying to pick the team," said Carrick, when the general plusses and minuses of the situation were put to him before his side's trip to Everton on Sunday.

"We're not just putting a squad together for one game on Sunday. We need a squad that's going to take us through the whole season.

"There's a whole picture in there that we need to balance. Sometimes it's to change during the game, sometimes it's game-to-game, sometimes you play every three or four days.

"Whoever plays in there, we are talking about adding to the squad and feeling we've got different partnerships and combinations we can rely on to get us through a season with unfortunate injuries or suspensions or whatever may come."

articles.title: Women's Super League: Arsenal and Chelsea prepare for first games in the WSL
articles.summary: With the Women's Super League season starting up, are Arsenal in a better position than Chelsea to challenge for the title?
articles.body:
Last season, Arsenal finished above Chelsea in the Women's Super League for the first time in seven years.

The last occasion was in 2018-19, the most recent title for the Gunners.

In between, Chelsea finished top of the pile for six straight seasons.

In 2025-26, while both trailed in the wake of eventual champions Manchester City, Arsenal leapfrogged their London rivals to finish second.

They also knocked the Blues out of the Women's Champions League in the quarter-finals.

So did those results signal a changing of the guard in the capital?

And what about London City Lionesses, who opened the WSL season with victory over Manchester United on Friday and now boast Spain superstar Alexia Putellas in their ranks?

Arsenal 'have real hunger' for WSL title

This summer, both Arsenal and Chelsea have experienced turnover in their squads.

The Gunners lost stalwarts Beth Mead and Katie McCabe among others but have freshened their team with England midfielder Georgia Stanway, Spain World Cup winner Ona Batlle and Switzerland captain Geraldine Reuteler among a glut of exciting signings.

At Stamford Bridge, Chelsea snapped up McCabe on a free transfer and splashed cash on Manchester United's Melvine Malard but can no longer call on Sam Kerr and Millie Bright, two defining players from their era of dominance.

With their latest quest for silverware getting started this weekend, it was Arsenal boss Renee Slegers who struck a more confident tone about her expectations for the season.

"We've been open about it - the WSL title is something we're going after," said Slegers, before her side open the season at Brighton on Sunday. "It's something where we really have our mind set.

"Of course there's a big belief in what we are doing, the quality that we possess and the different tools we have to use. There's a real hunger."

Sunday's game offers Arsenal an early return to Broadfield Stadium in Crawley, where their bid to chase down Manchester City last season was ended by a 1-1 draw against Brighton in May.

A number of similar results cost Arsenal, particularly at the beginning of the year, and Slegers is determined to avoid lightning striking twice.

"We've spoken about it with the staff, the captains, the player group," she said. "Everyone is aware of it. We know the hurdles we had last year - and that's what we're working towards.

"The quality of players that we have here, there's so many things that we can bring to a game now. I'm really happy about it."

And is this her strongest squad at Arsenal?

At Chelsea, manager Sonia Bompastor was less bullish about her side's chances of regaining the WSL title.

"I'm trying to be as honest as possible. Chelsea is in a transitional phase," Bompastor said. "We are rebuilding, regenerating the squad.

"As much as I know my job is to win many games and to win trophies and I'm desperate for that - but it also takes time for the squad to gel together."

"The DNA for Chelsea is to win and we want to make sure we go as far as possible in every competition."

Chelsea open the season against Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime, live on BBC One, and have been installed as favourites by Opta's supercomputer, which gives the Blues a 39.9% chance , external of winning the league.

Not that Bompastor is paying any attention.

"I remember sitting here last season and someone told me the same," she said. "Our percentage was higher than this season! I'm not too focused on what numbers and what is coming from AI or computers."

She believes that this season will be the toughest yet and, while acknowledging the significant threat from champions Manchester City, she says challengers will come from all directions.

"The beauty in this league is that many clubs are in a position to win the title," Bompastor said. "It was already the most competitive league in the world and it's becoming stronger every season.

"Every game is so difficult but that's good. I'm excited for it."

One of those could be London City, who after finishing sixth in their maiden WSL season have spent big this summer.

Their goal is likely to be challenging the established elite in the WSL, although ambitious owner Michelle Kang will not settle for that.

She has previously told BBC Sport that London City "have an aspiration to be at the top of the game" and starting the season with a convincing performance against Manchester United lends credence to that plan.

articles.title: Qué pasó en Mestalla... un 5 de septiembre de 1976: el primer gol de Kempes con el Valencia fue en casa
articles.standfirst: Primer partido de Liga de la 1976-77 contra el Celta, el delantero argentino despunta y brilla con dos goles, los primeros como jugador blanquinegro
articles.summary: Primer partido de Liga de la 1976-77 contra el Celta, el delantero argentino despunta y brilla con dos goles, los primeros como jugador blanquinegro
articles.body: Mario Alberto Kempes empezó con el idilio del gol en el Valencia y en el primer partido de la temporada ante el Celta de Vigo. Después de un debut aciago nada más llegar en el ya famoso Trofeo Naranja, donde todo lo que el ariete argentino hizo salió a la inversa, pero en el primer choque oficial del club de Mestalla dio buena cuenta del olfato goleador del 'matador'. El Valencia se impuso a los vigueses por dos goles a cero ambos tantos obra del argentino. Este partido se disputó un domingo por la noche en Mestalla para erradicar el sofoco de la temperatura veraniega en la comunidad. Fue el 5 de septiembre de 1976. Aquel partido empezó un domingo y acabó un lunes pero Mario Alberto Kempes dio buena cuenta de lo que venía por delante con sus dos primeros goles, como valencianista y además en su estadio. El primer gol del argentino en el Valencia llegó de la siguiente manera: corría el minuto 2 de la segunda parte cuando Adorno centra un balón al área que devuelve Tirapu desde el otro lado hacia el centro del área... y allí estaba el 'Matador'. Esperando el balón. La peinó limpiamente a la red. 1-0. El primero de una larga lista. El Valencia formó en aquel partido del debut liguero con Pepe Balaguer, como portero, con Carrete, Cerveró, Jesús Martínez, Ángel Castellanos, Tirapu, Saura, Johnny Rep, Lobo Diarte, Adorno y Mario Kempes. Mario Alberto Kempes anotó un total de 149 goles en 246 partidos oficiales desde 1976 a 1984 salvo una etapa en la que jugó en River Plate pero tuvo que regresar porque la entidad argentina no pudo hacer frente al pago del traspaso. Conquistó tres títulos con el club: la Copa del Rey de 1979, la Recopa de Europa de la temporada 1979-80 y la Supercopa de Europa de 1980-81.

articles.title: La BMV patina en la primera cuesta
articles.standfirst: La delantera del Madrid, con un Mbappé especialmente negado, se queda a cero en la rampa inicial
articles.summary: La delantera del Madrid, con un Mbappé especialmente negado, se queda a cero en la rampa inicial
articles.body: Al Real Madrid le falló la delantera en el primer test serio de la temporada. No fue por falta de situaciones de gol. Las hubo de casi todos los colores, incluyendo tres remates a la madera, un penalti fallado y una exhibición de Valles, que acabó desquiciando a los delanteros de José Mourinho. Sobre todo a Kylian Mbappé, al que le negó el gol de casi todas las formas imaginables, culminando con la parada del penalti en el minuto 94. A punto estuvo Mbappé de tener la oportunidad de repetirlo, pero Hernández Hernández decidió lo contrario. Mbappé fue la imagen de la frustración blanca, con un buen puñado de ocasiones muy claras, en especial una doble en la primera parte, que abortaron entre Valles y su defensa. El meta también se interpuso a dos buenos cabezazos de Bellingham y Espí, firmando una de las mejores noches de su carrera, si no la mejor. Con todo, el delantero valenciano sí logró batir al meta local, también muy cerca del minuto 90, pero la acción fue invalidada por un fuera de juego anterior. Sin duda, ambas decisiones serán combustible para la polémica en las próximas horas. No estuvo bien Mbappé, y tampoco lo estuvo Bellingham, que pareció cansado casi desde el mismo arranque del partido, como si el calor sofocante de La Cartuja le estuviera afectando en exceso. Eso no quiere decir que no corriera ni lo intentará, pero al margen de un par detalles no fue ni de lejos el jugador punzante de los primeros partidos de la temporada. Pese a todo, sólo Valles y el travesaño le impidieron volver a mojar. Tampoco Vini tuvo una noche apacible. Se midió en un buen puñado de ocasiones a Bellerín, y el lateral del Betis le ganó la práctica totalidad de los duelos. Pese a ello, su insistencia le dio para forzar el penalti que pudo ser el empate de los blancos, y, al igual que sus dos compañeros de ataque, se encontró con la madera tras una gran acción del ataque blanco en el primer acto. Aunque el partido del Madrid no fue malo, lo cierto es que la falta de acierto de sus delanteros penalizó a los blancos, que se quedaron a cero por primera vez en la temporada, incluyendo los seis partidos de pretemporada. Lo malo es que el patinazo llegó en la primera cuesta seria que afrontaba el equipo, el primer test de nivel y a sólo unos pocos días del estreno europeo del Madrid. En ese partido, el problema será la falta de medios, con hasta tres jugadores sancionados. El martes se verá si el ataque puede minimizarlo.

articles.title: El Di Stéfano estrena 'muro'
articles.standfirst: El central Oscar Naasei, que firmó un notable debut ante el Teruel, se presenta en Valdebebas
articles.summary: El central Oscar Naasei, que firmó un notable debut ante el Teruel, se presenta en Valdebebas
articles.body: Oscar Naasei, el flamante fichaje del Castilla procedente del Granada, será una de las grandes atracciones este sábado en el primer partido de la temporada del Castilla en el Di Stéfano ante el Juventud Torremolinos (12:00 h, Orange TV, Movistar Primera Federación, Dazn, Football Club y FanPlay TV). El central tuvo un notable debut en la visita a Teruel, donde formó pareja de centrales con Mario Rivas y juntos levantaron un 'muro' defensivo que acabó con el filial firmando un empate sin goles en la primera jornada liguera. Una actuación que pone en duda el regreso de Joan Martínez a la titularidad, tras ser suplente por sorpresa frente al Teruel por las opciones que tenía para salir con el mercado de fichajes aún abierto. Julián López de Lerma tiene una decisión complicada, con Mario Rivas entrando en convocatorias del primer equipo, Naasei brillando en su debut y en su condición de fichaje estrella del filial y un Joan Martínez que es considerado por muchos en el club el defensa con más proyección de futuro y que la pasada temporada ya fue el gran jefe de la defensa del Castilla siendo todavía juvenil. Es, sin duda, una de las grandes dudas en el once del Castilla, una vez que en el resto del equipo no se esperan muchos cambios. En los laterales mandan Fortea y Aguado y la opción de una variación en el equipo inicial se abre en la medular, donde Mesonero y Roberto Martín optan al puesto de Manex, junto a Cestero y Pol Fortuny. No se espera en la convocatoria del Castilla a un Sergio Martínez al que Mou, una vez incluido en la lista A de la Champions, querrá proteger para el duelo ante el Inter ante las numerosas bajas en el centro del campo. El filial blanco, poco acertado de cara a puerta en su estreno liguero, se aferra a su tridente ofensivo para encontrar el camino del gol que le lleve a su primera victoria de la temporada. Rachad, que falló un penalti ante el Teruel, tiene una cuenta pendiente que quiere saldar; un 'renacido' Leiva, que le ganó la partida a Yáñez en el primer once, quiere seguir con su particular remontada tras su sobresaliente actuación el pasado fin de semana; y la sensación Ciria buscará ser ese jugador diferencia que le ha llevado a ser 'niño' de Mou durante toda la pretemporada.

articles.title: Oyarzabal alcanzará en Elche a Kortabarria en el noveno puesto de jugadores históricos
articles.standfirst: El actual capitán txuriurdin disputará su encuentro oficial número 442 y esta misma temporada podría rebasar también a Gajate, López Ufarte y Fuentes y colocarse sexto
articles.summary: El actual capitán txuriurdin disputará su encuentro oficial número 442 y esta misma temporada podría rebasar también a Gajate, López Ufarte y Fuentes y colocarse sexto
articles.body: Mikel Oyarzabal ascenderá este lunes en Elche un puesto más en la clasificación de futbolistas con más partidos oficiales con la Real Sociedad, al alcanzar los 442 que tienen en el noveno lugar a Inaxio Kortabarria, otra de las leyendas del club txuriurdin por tener en su palmarés, entre otros, los dos títulos de Liga. El actual capitán, que ya lo juega todo pese a su corta preparación, podría llegar este curso hasta la sexta posición. Oyarzabal, parece mentira, va camino del undécimo aniversario de su debut con la Real y en Primera división, el 25 de octubre de 2025, y desde entonces y pese a la grave lesión que sufrió en 2022 y que le tuvo casi 10 meses de baja, ha logrado ir haciendo una carrera que le tiene ya como una de las leyendas de la entidad, pese a que todavía le resten unos años más en activo. El actual número 10 ha ido cumpliendo 100, 200, 300 y 400 encuentros, con los dos títulos de Copa como fechas más significativas de todos ellos, entrando en el top ten de históricos el pasado mes de marzo, cuando llegó al 427, la cifra que durante muchos años había tenido en el décimo lugar a Mikel Aramburu, y añadiendo desde entonces partidos hasta situarse actualmente en los 441, a uno de los 442 de la novena plaza de Inaxio Kortabarria. Todo apunta a que Oyarzabal llegará y rebasará esa cantidad jugando de media punta, el nuevo puesto que ya a finales del curso pasado dejamos entrever en el que podía actuar y en el que ha empezado a hacerlo en este, pese a volver a la Real tras ser el pichichi de la selección campeona del Mundo actuando de delantero. Por cierto, hablando de goles, con 133 tiene sólo por delante los 162 de Jesús Satrústegui para ser el máximo realizador. El capitán de los txuriurdin podría pasar esta misma temporada los 469 partidos de Agustín Gajate, los 474 de Roberto López Ufarte y los 495 de Miguel Fuentes, y llegar a una sexta posición de una clasificación de históricos en la que ya sólo tendría por delante a Xabi Prieto (532), Luis Arconada (551), Jesús Mari Zamora (588), Juan Antonio Larrañaga (589) y Alberto Gorriz (599).

articles.title: 'Flipe' Luis
articles.standfirst: Supera al PSG 1-2, al que ya mete 7 puntos, y es el primer técnico del Mónaco en ganar sus cinco primeros partidos
articles.summary: Supera al PSG, al que ya mete 7 puntos
articles.body: El arranque de Filipe Luis en el Mónaco ya solo puede tildarse de histórico, tras su victoria ayer por 1-2 ante el PSG de Luis Enrique en el Parque de los Príncipes. El conjunto dirigido por el ex lateral del Atlético de Madrid, había firmado un pleno de victorias en sus dos primeros encuentros, ambas con la portería a cero, y ahora ya es completo: tres victorias, liderato en la Ligue 1 y el campeón de Europa... a 7 puntos. El primer entrenador de la historia del equipo galo en ganar sus cinco primeros partidos si se añaden los dos de la fase previa de Conference ante el Górnik polaco. Y viene, en su primer año como técnico, ganar Libertadores, Brasileirão, Copa de Brasil y Supercopa. Un flipe, aunque lo venía cocinando de lejos. Fue entrenado por técnicos como Jorge Jesus, Simeone y Mourinho durante su carrera, y ha reconocido que ya de jugador tomaba nota de ellos para ser él entrenador en un futuro, sus tácticas, entrenamientos y gestión de plantilla. Sus chicos, que arrancaron perdiendo el partido en París, le dieron la vuelta en la segunda parte. "En el descanso intenté ser honesto con lo que estaba pasando en el campo. Para mí, estábamos perdiendo, pero estábamos jugando bien. Tuvimos ocasiones, no muy claras, pero las tuvimos. Corregí varios detalles de la presión y con balón, realicé unos matices y los jugadores lo entendieron", afirmó el técnico. Teze por Vanderson en el ataque, al que se lanzó el cuadro del principado, sin complejos, aun dejando desguarnecida la defensa. Y lo lograron con Nazinho e Idumbo, pese a que Lucho, recién renovado junto a Fabian, sacó a Ferran con el empate buscando de nuevo un gol milagrero. No pudo, ni el PSG ganar desde que comenzó la liga. Con todo, Filipe se deshizo en elogios hacia su homólogo en el banquillo parisino, Luis Enrique. “Se lo he dicho tras el partido: para mí no es el mejor del mundo, es uno de los mejores entrenadores en la historia. Se lo dije. He copiado muchas cosas de Luis Enrique. Le he estado siguiendo durante tiempo. Cómo se comportan sus jugadores y sus equipos. Para mí es un placer jugar contra él y un honor competir contra él”.

articles.title: Everton: David Moyes says he has never spoken to owner Dan Friedkin
articles.summary: Everton manager David Moyes says he has never met or spoken to the club's owner Dan Friedkin.
articles.body:
David Moyes says he has never met or spoken to Everton owner Dan Friedkin since returning as manager in January 2025.

Friedkin is head of The Friedkin Group, which runs the club from its base in Houston, but has not attended a home game since completing a takeover of the club in December 2024.

How the club is run and who is responsible for making key decisions came under close scrutiny during the summer transfer window.

Speaking to reporters before Everton 's match against Manchester United on Sunday, Moyes reiterated his commitment to the club despite a chaotic end to the window.

When asked if he had ever met or spoken to Friedkin in the 20 months since he was reappointed as manager, Moyes' answer was a simple "No".

Friedkin leaves the day-to-day running of the club to his son-in-law Rishi Majithia, who works in tandem with chief executive Angus Kinnear.

"My real contact is Angus," said Moyes. "Angus is the one who I would go to see. Rishi is the next one and then the head of the Friedkin family in America.

"I don't really get any direct conversations with them, but I do through Rishi, he is the one I would speak to."

Fans reacted angrily during last Saturday's match at Bournemouth following news the club had accepted a £40m bid from Nottingham Forest for one of their prized assets, England Under-19s midfielder Harrison Armstrong.

Everton eventually pulled out of the deal, but supporters remain frustrated by decisions made by the board in the remainder of the transfer window.

Beto was sold to Fiorentina on deadline day on Tuesday, before the club had secured a replacement striker, with USA forward Folarin Balogun then backing out of a move to Everton from Monaco at the 11th hour on Tuesday.

Everton finished the transfer window with a squad of just 18 senior players, including only one striker, one right-back and one left-back.

Moyes aligned himself with Everton fans last weekend when asked about plans to sell Armstrong, saying the club was "managed by an Evertonian" and "supporters aren't always wrong".

And he acknowledged on Friday that there was work to do done on the club's structure behind the scenes: "We've got new owners in who are still feeling their way in the club. I think if we get to know each other more it will get better."

But the former Manchester United and West Ham boss said he would not walk away from the challenge of unifying a club that he led to a succession of top-five finishes in the Premier League between 2002 and 2013 in his first stint as manager.

" Everton 's different," said Moyes, when asked if he had considered quitting. "I wouldn't have come back for anybody but Everton .

"I think the club here has had enough days where the people find a way of recovering. People saw the face of Evertonians last week and it can be really powerful. I would expect them to be really powerful now.

"But powerful for the team, powerful for the players. What we're going to need from them is extra because we're short, so we need them. If they're not with us, then it's terrible. And they are with us, I believe they are with us."

articles.title: Swansea City v Wrexham: Eyes on big prize as Welsh duo collide
articles.summary: Swansea City and Wrexham meet in a mouthwatering Welsh derby with stakes high as both clubs eye the Premier League.
articles.body:
Swansea City and Wrexham will meet in the league for the 33rd time this Saturday evening.

Rarely, if ever, can there have been a more eagerly anticipated encounter between two clubs who are rivals, of sorts, despite being from opposite corners of Wales.

The fixture which matters most to Swansea fans is against Cardiff City, their neighbours in the south of the country.

For Wrexham, meanwhile, local squabbles with Chester and Shrewsbury Town have traditionally been the games which have come with the greatest significance.

But Swansea against Wrexham has a derby feel too, even though the cities are more than 100 miles apart.

And this particular meeting comes with increased stakes because both clubs have eyes on the Premier League.

Wrexham ended last season as top dogs in Wales, with Phil Parkinson's side finishing seventh in the Championship and Vitor Matos' Swansea seven points worse off in 11th.

It was the first time since 2000-01 - when they came 10th in what is now League One - that Wrexham had finished a campaign as the best-placed Welsh side in the English pyramid.

After three successive promotions, Wrexham, who beat Swansea at home in March after losing the reverse fixture last December, narrowly missed out on a play-off chance in May.

But their best-in-Wales status was another sign of the extraordinary progress they have made since Hollywood stars Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac took charge of the club in 2021.

Cardiff City's promotion from League One means that for only the third time, Wales' three heavyweight clubs are together in the second tier this season.

Given that the three teams have never competed together in the top flight - Swansea and Cardiff have met there in just one season, while Wrexham have not played at the highest level - a three-way Championship scrap is a big deal in Wales.

But to an extent the fight to be crowned the nation's leading team is a sideshow, with both Swansea and Wrexham chasing a greater prize.

Most observers would regard Cardiff as outsiders to feature in the promotion race next spring as they look to re-establish themselves at second-tier level.

But the picture is different for Swansea and Wrexham, who both showed considerable ambition in the transfer market for the second year in a row this summer as they look to compete with the Championship's top sides.

These are very early days in the season, but the signs from Swansea have been encouraging, with a tally of 10 points from four games putting them on top of the table.

They have conceded only one league goal so far - the best record in the EFL - while Matos' team produced some of Swansea's best football in years during Tuesday's win over Watford.

The Swans are in buoyant mood, while Wrexham should make the journey south with renewed confidence following their midweek triumph at Millwall.

The Red Dragons endured a concerning start to the season, with chances going begging in their draws with Cardiff and Watford before they were deservedly beaten at home by a Birmingham City team who were under pressure to deliver a result.

But the mood at the Racecourse has lightened significantly thanks to that emphatic victory over a Millwall side who are widely tipped to compete for promotion once more this season.

Another away success this weekend would make this a huge week for Parkinson and his players.

A home win, by contrast, would add to the feeling that Matos' new-look team could end Swansea's run of five successive mid-table Championship finishes by securing a place in the newly extended play-offs.

The fact that Swansea against Wrexham has been selected for a Saturday evening live television slot says something about the interest in the game, which will be watched well beyond Wales' border.

There will be plenty looking on from the United States, for example, given the owners of the two clubs.

In the red corner are Reynolds and Mac, whose Welcome to Wrexham television series has turned what was a non-league football club into a global brand.

And in the white corner are Snoop Dogg, Luka Modric and Martha Stewart, all of whom have become co-owners at Swansea over the past 17 months.

The set-up at each club is different, with Reynolds and Mac the majority owners of Wrexham while Swansea's big names in the boardroom hold only minor stakes.

But the idea at Swansea, whose majority owners are American businessmen Brett Cravatt and Jason Cohen, is to "do a Wrexham" by raising their profile through the non-playing stars associated with the club.

Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

Listen to the latest Wrexham interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

The theory is that increased profile means increased income, which in turn allows more money to be spent on strengthening the team.

At this stage, it is difficult to judge what difference Snoop and Co have made.

But what is not in question is that for a second successive year, Swansea showed significant ambition in the transfer market.

Eight years after a golden period in their history ended with relegation from the Premier League, Swansea look like a club determined to have a serious go at getting back to the highest level.

For Wrexham, the goal is to join the elite for the first time, with their intent even more apparent based on the head-turning sums they have spent on transfers since promotion to the Championship in 2025.

We wait to discover whether either club has sufficient resources to mount a genuine push for the Premier League this season.

And while nothing will be decided in early September, there may be a few clues on offer this weekend.

articles.title: Fenerbahce’s Greenwood, Guendouzi handed fines and bans after brawl at Lyon
articles.summary: Fights between players and coaching staff broke out after the Turkish side won the Champions League playoff second leg.
articles.body:
Fenerbahce duo Mason Greenwood and Matteo Guendouzi have been suspended and fined for their part in the chaotic scenes after their club’s Champions League playoff second leg against Lyon.

Last month’s 2-1 victory for Fenerbahce in France meant the Turkish side progressed 3-2 on aggregate, and, after the final whistle, Greenwood and Guendouzi, who both previously played for Lyon’s bitter rivals Marseille, were involved in a brawl with players and coaching staff from both sides.

Former Arsenal midfielder Guendouzi has been suspended “for a total of four UEFA club competition matches for which he would otherwise be eligible, for insulting others present at the match, provoking spectators and for violating the basic rules of decent conduct”, UEFA announced in a decision made public on Friday evening.

Two of the matches are subject to a “one-year probationary period”, European football’s governing body added in the statement.

Guendouzi, who was also fined 50,000 euros ($58,000), was found guilty, among other things, of giving the middle finger to Lyon supporters and of provocations that led to a scuffle after the match.

His English teammate Mason Greenwood, formerly of Manchester United, received a one-match suspended ban and was fined 30,000 euros ($35,000) for “violating the basic rules of decent conduct”.

articles.title: Steve Clarke needed to give SFA 'a little shove' for new contract
articles.summary: Steve Clarke says he had to cajole the Scottish FA into handing him a new contract as national head coach shortly before the World Cup finals this summer because he felt the governing body was hedging its bets.
articles.body:
Former Scotland boss Steve Clarke says he had to cajole the Scottish FA into handing him a new contract as national head coach shortly before the World Cup finals this summer because he felt the governing body was hedging its bets.

But the 63-year-old insists he nevertheless always planned to resign if he failed to lead Scotland beyond the group stage for the first time.

Speaking for the first time since the tournament in the Americas, Clarke was being interviewed by former Chelsea and Scotland team-mate Pat Nevin at Spartans Community Foundation dinner in Edinburgh.

Asked about his exit from the job despite the four-year contract he signed on the eve of the tournament, and quoted by The Scotsman, he said: "It was never really a change of mind.

"I am quite a complex person. I wanted to control my narrative."

Clark added: "Obviously we got to March and I hadn't been offered a new contract, which I thought was pretty strange. You start to think are they hedging their bets a little bit, waiting on the tournament in the summer.

"So I did a little bit in the media in March to give the SFA a little shove. We negotiated non-stop from the beginning of April really to the middle of May, just before the Curacao game.

"And I said to them if we don't agree a new contract before we go to the World Cup then I will say I am leaving the job. They panicked a little bit and gave me the new contract.

"It was like drawing teeth trying to get it over the line. But we got it over the line anyway.

"But I always knew in my head that if we did not get out of the group stage then I would probably leave. The only way I would have stayed on is if they had been three fantastic games and they went against you."

Scotland beat Haiti 1-0 but lost by the same score to Morocco before a 3-0 loss to Brazil left them waiting for an unlikely series of results to allow them to progress as one of the better third-place sides.

"We had to stay for four or five days [in Charlotte], the longest four or five days ever just sitting and waiting, knowing you are going home because the goal difference was not good enough," he recalled.

"I knew we needed four points. I got hammered in the media for saying that. Somebody hammered me for saying, 'nah, that's us, we are going home'. But I was right."

Clarke revealed he spoke to several senior players following the Brazil game and sensed that they needed to hear a different voice if they are to make history by reaching the knockout stage at Euro 2028.

Meantime, he spoke to new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli last week to wish him well and believes "even Scotland" cannot fail to qualify given two spots in the finals will be reserved for the best-ranked host who have not qualified as a group winner or runner-up.
